examples: Bank employees are strictly forbidden to divulge customer account details.
The journalist refused to divulge the name of her source, even when the court ordered her to.

meaning: Easily managed or trained; submissive
trick: 'Doc'+'Smile' — Doctor की बात Smile से मानने वाला सीधा मरीज़।
examples: The trainees were docile and followed every instruction without question.
The docile elephant stood calmly while the children climbed on its back, obeying every word of the keeper.

hindi: दृढ़ / हठी / हार न मानने वाला
meaning: Persistent and determined; refusing to give up
trick: 'Dog'+'Zid' — बुलडॉग अगर किसी चीज़ को पकड़ ले तो छोड़ता नहीं, वैसे ही अपनी धुन का पक्का रहना।
examples: His dogged determination helped him crack the RBI Grade B exam on his third try.
With dogged effort, the climbers pushed through the snowstorm and finally reached the summit at noon.

meaning: Asserting opinions as if they were unquestionably true
trick: 'Dog'+'Mat' — डॉग मैट पर बैठ जाए तो हटने से मना कर देता है।
examples: He is too dogmatic to accept any modern changes in the banking sector.
The dogmatic coach insisted his method was the only right one and refused to hear any other idea.

meaning: Exhibiting sorrow or distress
trick: 'Dollar'+'Loss' — Dollar में Loss, निवेशक दुखी।
examples: The dolorous news of the founder's death spread quickly.
A dolorous cry rose from the crowd as the rescue team brought out the bodies from the mine.

hindi: सुप्त / निष्क्रिय (जो अभी चालू न हो)
meaning: Inactive but capable of being activated
trick: 'Door'+'Mat' — डोरमैट पर पड़े-पड़े सो जाना; जिस खाते में 2 साल से लेन-देन न हो वो Dormant (सुप्त) है।
examples: You need to submit fresh KYC documents to reactivate your dormant bank account.
The volcano had lain dormant for centuries, so the villagers were shocked when it rumbled to life.

meaning: Brave, persistent, and resolute
trick: 'Dau' — Doughty (डाउ-टी) ≈ दाऊ (बलराम) जैसे वीर और ताकतवर, जो किसी से नहीं डरते।
examples: The doughty soldiers defended the border for three long weeks.
The doughty old farmer kept ploughing his dry field year after year, never losing hope of rain.

meaning: Favoring gentle or accommodative policies
trick: 'Dove' (कबूतर) = नरम; RBI Dovish = रेट घटाना।
examples: Investors expected a dovish approach from the Federal Reserve.
The dovish minister urged talks and patience, saying war would bring only suffering to both countries.

meaning: Hesitating or doubting; suspicious
trick: 'Dooba' — जिस स्कीम में पैसा डूबा हुआ लगे वो संदिग्ध होती है।
examples: The bank rejected his loan due to dubious financial records.
Looking dubious, the shopkeeper held the banknote to the light and asked whether the customer had another.

meaning: Deceitful double-dealing
trick: 'Duplicate' — मुंह पर कुछ और पीठ पीछे कुछ और बोलने वाला दोगलापन और धोखा।
examples: The company was blacklisted after its duplicity in tax filing was caught.
The spy's duplicity came to light when officers found he was sending secrets to two different countries.

meaning: To gradually decrease in size or amount
trick: 'Din Dhale' — जैसे-जैसे दिन ढलता है, रोशनी धीरे-धीरे कम होती जाती है।
examples: The bank's customer base began to dwindle after the service charges were hiked.
As the drought continued, the water in the village well began to dwindle to a muddy puddle.

meaning: Irritable and bad-tempered, often from indigestion
trick: 'Dis'+'Pepsi' — ज़्यादा Pepsi पीकर पेट Disturb और मूड चिड़चिड़ा।
examples: His dyspeptic remarks at breakfast annoyed the entire family.
The dyspeptic old professor snapped at his students all morning and blamed the canteen food for his mood.

meaning: Overflowing with enthusiasm and excitement
trick: 'E'+'Bullet' — नई बुलेट बाइक गिफ्ट में पाकर लड़का जोशीला हो गया।
examples: The stock market was ebullient after the favorable budget announcement.
The ebullient crowd danced in the streets after the home team won the national championship.

meaning: An outburst of sudden strong emotion
trick: 'Ebullient' (उबलता) — उबलते हुए गुस्से का फूटना।
examples: An ebullition of anger followed the surprise announcement.
A sudden ebullition of joy swept the hall when the principal announced that classes were cancelled for a week.

meaning: Unconventional and slightly strange
trick: 'Ex'+'Center' — Center (केंद्र) से Ex (बाहर) रहने वाला अजीब।
examples: The eccentric scientist had 27 cats and wore a lab coat to dinner.
Her eccentric uncle painted his house purple and walked his pet goat through the market every morning.

meaning: The process of shedding old skin or shell in animals
trick: 'Exit'+'Dress' — सांप अपनी पुरानी Dress (खाल) से Exit करता है।
examples: Ecdysis helps insects grow larger by shedding their outer shell.
Zoology students watched the snake go through ecdysis, slowly wriggling out of its dull, dry skin.

meaning: A level or rank in an organization
trick: 'Aish'+'Lawn' — ऊँचे Echelon (पद) वाले अफ़सर Lawn वाले बंगलों में ऐश करते हैं।
examples: These policy decisions are made only by the upper echelons of the ministry.
Only those in the higher echelon of the army were invited to the secret briefing at headquarters.

hindi: विविध / विभिन्न स्रोतों से लिया हुआ
meaning: Selecting from a variety of sources
trick: 'Ek'+'Collect' — एक-एक करके अलग-अलग जगहों से आइडिया कलेक्ट करना।
examples: The mutual fund portfolio has an eclectic mix of large and small cap stocks.
Her eclectic taste in music ranges from folk songs and jazz to opera and modern electronic beats.

meaning: To obscure or overshadow something
trick: 'A'+'Clips' — जब सूरज को कुछ Clips (क्लिप) करके ढक दिया जाए।
examples: The success of the new product will eclipse the company's previous failures.
The tall office tower seemed to eclipse the little temple that once dominated the skyline of the town.

meaning: To bubble up; to show high spirits
trick: 'Fizz' + 'escence' — Cold Drink की तरह बुलबुले उठना।
examples: The team effervesced with excitement after winning the deal.
The children effervesced with laughter as the magician pulled a rabbit out of his empty hat.

meaning: Bubbly and enthusiastic
trick: 'Fizz' — Fizz (बुलबुले) वाली Cold Drink की तरह जोश भरा।
examples: Her effervescent personality made her the star of the team.
The effervescent host kept the party lively with jokes, games and an endless supply of warm smiles.

meaning: A sculpture or model of a person, often for protest
trick: 'Figure'+'जी' — दशहरे पर रावण-जी का Figure (पुतला) जलाते हैं, वही Effigy है।
examples: Protestors burned an effigy of the corrupt official outside the parliament.
Angry villagers hung an effigy of the cruel landlord from a tree and set it on fire.

hindi: फूल खिलना / सतह पर पाउडर जमना
meaning: A powdery surface bloom; the state of flowering
trick: 'Flower' — पौधे पर फूल खिलना, या गीली दीवार पर सफ़ेद पाउडर का फूल जैसा खिल जाना।
examples: The efflorescence on the old wall indicated rising damp.
White efflorescence appeared on the brick walls of the school after the monsoon soaked the building.

meaning: Insolent or impertinent boldness
trick: 'Front'+'तेरी' — गलती करके भी Front (सामने) आकर बहस? तेरी हिम्मत! यानी ढीठता।
examples: The fraudster had the effrontery to ask for another loan after defaulting on the first.
He had the effrontery to walk into the manager's room and demand a promotion on his first day.

meaning: Believing in the equality of all people
trick: 'Equal' — जो समाज में हर इंसान को Equal (समान) अधिकार देने में विश्वास रखे।
examples: Financial inclusion aims to build a more egalitarian society.
The school followed an egalitarian rule: every child, rich or poor, sat on the same bench and ate together.

meaning: Outstandingly bad; shocking
trick: 'E'+'Great'+'Lie' — जो Lie (झूठ) Great (बहुत बड़ा) हो वो भयानक गलती है।
examples: The auditor discovered an egregious error in the balance sheet.
The newspaper printed an egregious mistake on its front page, naming the wrong team as the winner.

meaning: A phantom; an idealized image
trick: 'Eye'+'Doll' — आँख में गुड़िया की भूतिया परछाई।
examples: The eidolon of his lost love haunted his dreams.
The old poet wrote of an eidolon of his mother that seemed to walk through the garden at dusk.

meaning: Extremely happy and excited
trick: 'Election' — इलेक्शन जीतने के बाद उम्मीदवार बहुत खुश होते हैं।
examples: She was elated when she received her joining letter from SBI.
The elated farmer danced in his field when the first rain clouds finally appeared after months of drought.

meaning: Expressing sorrow, especially for the dead
trick: 'Alley'+'जय' — गली में जय का जनाज़ा, सब शोक में।
examples: An elegiac tone pervaded the farewell message from the retiring director.
The poem had an elegiac mood, mourning the village elders who had passed away over the years.

meaning: To draw out a response or information
trick: 'List' — पुलिस ने पूछताछ करके चोर के मुंह से सारे साथियों की List (जानकारी) बाहर निकलवा ली।
examples: The survey was designed to elicit honest feedback from bank customers.
A good teacher knows how to elicit answers from shy students without making them feel afraid.

hindi: वाग्मी / स्पष्ट और प्रभावशाली बोलने वाला
meaning: Fluent, persuasive, and moving in speech
trick: 'Hello'+'Fluent' — जो "Hello" से ही Fluent और असरदार बोले, वो वाग्मी है।
examples: The CEO gave an eloquent speech that inspired all employees.
The eloquent young lawyer moved the entire courtroom to tears with her closing argument for the orphans.

meaning: To make something clear; to explain
trick: 'Loose' — उलझी गाँठ Loose करके साफ़ समझाना।
examples: The RBI governor elucidated the objectives of the new policy.
The teacher drew a diagram on the board to elucidate how the water cycle really works.

hindi: पकड़ में न आने वाला / दुर्लभ / चकमा देने वाला
meaning: Difficult to find, catch, or achieve
trick: 'Illusion' — जो माया या परछाई की तरह हाथ बढ़ाते ही फिसल जाए और पकड़ में न आए।
examples: Profitability remains elusive for many new e- commerce startups.
Sleep remained elusive that night, and he lay awake listening to the rain tapping on the tin roof.

hindi: अत्यंत दुबला-पतला / कमजोर (भूख या बीमारी से)
meaning: Abnormally thin and weak
trick: 'Mess'+'Ate' — हॉस्टल का Mess छोड़ा, कुछ Ate (खाया) नहीं, तो शरीर अत्यंत दुबला हो गया।
examples: The rescue team found a herd of emaciated cattle in the drought-hit village.
The emaciated stray dog was nursed back to health by the kind family who found it near the railway track.

meaning: To make more attractive by adding decorative details
trick: 'Bell'+'Polish' — दिवाली पर घर में घंटियां (Bell) लगाकर और Polish करके सुंदर सजाना।
examples: Do not embellish your resume with fake skills before the interview.
The old fisherman loved to embellish his tales, so the fish he caught grew bigger every time he told the story.

meaning: To steal money entrusted to one's care
trick: 'Em'+'बेइज़्ज़त' — Employee ने बैंक का पैसा गबन किया, पकड़ा गया तो पूरी बेइज़्ज़ती हुई।
examples: The cashier was arrested for trying to embezzle bank funds.
The treasurer was jailed for trying to embezzle money that the temple committee had collected for the festival.

hindi: मुलायम करने वाला / शांत करने वाला
meaning: Soothing or calming
trick: 'मुलायम' — मुलायम क्रीम जो जलन शांत करे, मुलायम बात जो गुस्सा शांत करे।
examples: Her emollient words helped calm the angry customer quickly.
The nurse spoke in an emollient tone, and the frightened child soon stopped crying in the clinic.

meaning: The ability to understand and share another's feelings
trick: 'Sympathy' का बड़ा भाई — जिसमें दूसरे का दर्द अपना लगे।
examples: Customer service agents must handle complaints with empathy.
Her empathy for the lonely patients made her the most loved nurse in the entire hospital ward.

meaning: Based on observation or experiment rather than theory
trick: 'Practical' — Theory नहीं, Practical करके देखा गया सच, यानी प्रयोग पर आधारित।
examples: The RBI relies on empirical data before deciding on interest rates.
The scientist trusted only empirical evidence, so she repeated the experiment five times before announcing the result.

meaning: To match or surpass by imitation
trick: 'Amul'+'Rate' — हर नई डेयरी कंपनी अमूल की सफलता की नकल करके उसके जैसा बनना चाहती है।
examples: Many developing nations are trying to emulate India's UPI payment model.
Young players often try to emulate their heroes by practising the same shots for hours every evening.

hindi: स्थानिक / किसी विशेष क्षेत्र तक सीमित
meaning: Native to or confined to a certain region
trick: 'In'+'Desh' — Pandemic पूरी दुनिया में फैलता है लेकिन Endemic सिर्फ किसी एक खास क्षेत्र तक सीमित रहता है।
examples: Malaria is endemic to certain tropical regions of the world.
Certain rare orchids are endemic to the hills of the north-east and grow nowhere else on earth.

meaning: To publicly declare approval or support
trick: Cheque के पीछे Sign = Endorsement — जिसके पीछे आप Sign करते हो, उसका समर्थन करते हो।
examples: The RBI endorsed the new digital lending guidelines.
The famous cricketer agreed to endorse the new brand of sports shoes in a television advertisement.

meaning: To make someone feel drained of energy
trick: 'Energy'+'Waste' — फालतू कामों में एनर्जी वेस्ट करोगे तो शरीर कमजोर हो जाएगा।
examples: The long stressful working hours began to enervate him.
The scorching afternoon heat began to enervate the marchers, who dragged their feet along the dusty road.

hindi: अधिकार देना / वोट का अधिकार देना
meaning: To give someone the right to vote
trick: 'Franchise' = अधिकार (Domino's Franchise = दुकान का अधिकार); Enfranchise = वोट का अधिकार देना।
examples: The new bill aims to enfranchise migrant workers in city elections.
In 1920 the new law aimed to enfranchise women, giving them a voice in choosing their leaders.

meaning: A person or thing that is mysterious or difficult to understand
trick: 'In' + 'Magic' — जादूगर का मैजिक कैसे हुआ, यह सबके लिए एक पहेली और रहस्यमयी बात होती है।
examples: The sudden resignation of the CEO remains an enigma to the employees.
The thief who vanished from the locked room remained an enigma to the police for many years.

meaning: A feeling of listlessness from lack of interest
trick: 'On'+'WiFi' — WiFi On, पर करने को कुछ नहीं = ऊब।
examples: The repetitive nature of data entry caused deep ennui among staff.
Stuck at the quiet railway station for hours, the passengers slipped into a mood of ennui and kept yawning.

meaning: To happen afterward as a result
trick: 'इन'+'सुई' — गलत Injection की सुई लगी, उसके बाद बुखार आ गया, यानी परिणामस्वरूप होना।
examples: A massive sell-off ensued after the RBI announced the rate hike.
After the loud thunderclap, a deep silence ensued, and then the children began to giggle nervously.

meaning: To pronounce words clearly and distinctly
trick: 'Announce' — Railway Announcer की तरह हर शब्द साफ़-साफ़ और स्पष्ट बोलना।
examples: The RBI governor enunciated the new policy measures clearly in his speech.
The newsreader was praised for how clearly she could enunciate every word, even the hardest names.

meaning: Lasting for a very short time
trick: 'E'+'Fever' — वायरल फीवर सिर्फ 2-3 दिन के लिए आता है।
examples: The spike in sales was ephemeral and dropped the next week.
Soap bubbles are ephemeral, shimmering for a moment in the sunlight before they pop and vanish.

hindi: अचानक ज्ञान की प्राप्ति / अचानक समझ आना
meaning: A sudden, profound realization
trick: 'Apple'+'Fell' — जब न्यूटन के सिर पर सेब गिरा तो अचानक गुरुत्वाकर्षण का दिव्य ज्ञान प्राप्त हुआ।
examples: While reading the customer complaints, the founder had an epiphany for a new banking app.
Watching the apple fall, the boy had a sudden epiphany about why everything on earth is pulled downward.

meaning: A nosebleed
trick: 'पिस्ता' — गर्मी में ज़्यादा पिस्ता खाया तो नाक से खून (नकसीर) आने लगा।
examples: Epistaxis is common in dry weather when the nasal membranes get dry.
The doctor said the child's frequent epistaxis was harmless and advised him to pinch his nose and lean forward.

meaning: Relating to or denoting the writing of letters
trick: 'Post' — Post (डाक) से जाने वाली चिट्ठियों से जुड़ा, यानी पत्रों से संबंधित।
examples: The novel was written in an epistolary format, using letters between the characters.
Her grandmother kept an epistolary friendship alive for forty years, trading handwritten letters with a pen friend abroad.

meaning: A perfect example of a quality
trick: 'A Picture of Me' — "ईमानदारी का सबसे अच्छा Example चाहिए? मेरी Picture देखो!"
examples: The new CEO is the epitome of professional excellence and integrity.
With her patience and generosity, the old teacher was the epitome of kindness in our little town.

meaning: Mental calmness under stress
trick: 'Equal'+'Enemy' — सामने Enemy हो तब भी दिमाग का बैलेंस Equal रखना।
examples: A good manager handles crisis situations with equanimity.
The pilot faced the storm with equanimity, speaking in a steady voice that calmed every passenger.

meaning: Relating to horses or horse riding
trick: 'इक्का' — इक्का (घोड़ा-गाड़ी / तांगा) चलाने वाला, यानी घुड़सवार; घोड़ों से जुड़ा।
examples: She won a gold medal in the equestrian event at the Olympics.
The equestrian club trains riders every Sunday, and the stables are always full of well-groomed horses.

meaning: Fair and impartial
trick: 'Equal' — सबको बराबर और बिना भेदभाव के हिस्सा देना यानी न्यायसंगत।
examples: The government aims for an equitable distribution of wealth across the country.
The elders agreed on an equitable plan to share the harvest, giving each family a fair portion.

meaning: Open to more than one interpretation
trick: 'Equal'+'Vocal' — दोनों तरफ Equal Vocal होने से बात अस्पष्ट हो जाती है।
examples: The management's equivocal statement left employees confused.
His equivocal reply, half yes and half no, left the interviewers unsure whether he actually wanted the job.

meaning: Irregular and unpredictable in behavior
trick: 'Error'+'Automatic' — जिस मशीन में अपने आप बार- बार Error आए वह अनियमित चलती है।
examples: Erratic monsoon rains often hurt agricultural production in India.
The old bus ran on an erratic schedule, sometimes arriving early and sometimes not turning up at all.

meaning: Having or showing great knowledge
trick: 'E'+'Read'+'Diet' — जिसकी डाइट ही किताबें पढ़ना हो वो पक्का विद्वान होगा।
examples: The professor wrote an erudite book on the Indian banking system.
The erudite scholar could quote ancient poems from memory and discuss history in six different languages.

meaning: Understood by only a small group with special knowledge
trick: 'Ishwar'+'Trick' — ईश्वर की माया बहुत गुप्त होती है, आम आदमी नहीं समझ सकता।
examples: The financial models used by hedge funds are highly esoteric.
The club's rules were so esoteric that only its oldest members could make sense of them.

meaning: To adopt or support a cause or belief
trick: 'Spouse' — जैसे इंसान अपने जीवनसाथी का साथ देता है वैसे किसी विचार या नीति का समर्थन करना।
examples: Modern economists espouse the use of green energy for sustainable growth.
The young activist continued to espouse the cause of clean rivers in every speech she delivered.

meaning: Respect and admiration
trick: 'Team' — पूरी Team जिसका आदर करे, उसका Esteem (सम्मान) बड़ा; Self-esteem = आत्मसम्मान।
examples: The retired bank chairman is held in high esteem by all employees.
The villagers held the old doctor in great esteem because he had treated them for free for decades.

meaning: Extremely delicate and light, seemingly not of this world
trick: 'Air'+'real' — हवा में तैरती परी जैसा हल्का, अलौकिक।
examples: The ethereal beauty of the mountains at sunrise left everyone speechless.
Her ethereal voice drifted through the temple courtyard like mist, and the listeners sat in silent wonder.

meaning: A speech of high praise, especially for the dead
trick: 'You'+'Log'+'Ji' — "आप लोग जी बहुत महान थे!" कहकर किसी के जाने के बाद उसकी प्रशंसा में भाषण देना।
examples: He delivered a touching eulogy at the tribute ceremony of the founder.
At the funeral, the grandson read a warm eulogy that praised his grandfather's kindness and humour.

meaning: A feeling of intense excitement and happiness
trick: 'UFO' — UFO देखकर लोग खुशी से पागल हो गए।
examples: There was market euphoria following the corporate tax cut.
A wave of euphoria swept through the stadium when the home team scored the winning goal in the last minute.

meaning: Quickly fading; fleeting
trick: 'E' + 'Vanescent' (Vanishing) — जल्दी गायब हो जाने वाला।
examples: The beauty of the cherry blossoms is evanescent, lasting only a week.
The rainbow was evanescent, glowing across the valley for a few minutes before the clouds swallowed it.

meaning: To make a problem or situation worse
trick: 'Extra'+'Baat' — लड़ाई के बीच में एक्स्ट्रा बातें बोलने से स्थिति और बदतर हो जाती है।
examples: Rising crude oil prices will exacerbate the country's trade deficit.
Shouting at the nervous child will only exacerbate his fear of speaking in front of the class.

meaning: Demanding great care, effort, or precision
trick: 'Exact'+'ing' — Exact (सटीक) से काम कराने वाला।
examples: The exacting standards of the RBI audit left no room for errors.
The exacting coach demanded perfect form from every swimmer and made them repeat each lap until it was flawless.

meaning: A country's treasury or national fund
trick: 'Extra'+'Cheque' — एक्स्ट्रा चेक सरकारी खजाने में जमा होगा।
examples: Subsidies place a huge financial burden on the national exchequer.
Many kings of old filled their royal exchequer by collecting taxes on grain, salt and trade caravans.

meaning: To clear someone of blame
trick: 'Ex'+'Culprit' — किसी को Culprit (अपराधी) की लिस्ट से बाहर निकाल देना यानी दोषमुक्त करना।
examples: The audit report helped exculpate the branch manager from all fraud charges.
New video evidence helped exculpate the young driver, who had been wrongly blamed for causing the crash.

meaning: Serving as a perfect model for others
trick: 'Example' — जो काम इतना अच्छा हो कि दूसरों के लिए Example बन जाए।
examples: He was awarded for his exemplary service in the rural banking sector.
The principal praised the girl's exemplary conduct, saying she had never missed a class or spoken rudely.

meaning: Requiring immediate action; urgent
trick: 'Emergency'+'Urgent' — ऐसा काम जो बहुत Urgent हो और जिसे तुरंत करना ज़रूरी हो।
examples: The central bank held a midnight meeting due to exigent market conditions.
The ship's captain made an exigent call for help when water began to pour into the engine room.

meaning: Very small; scanty
trick: 'एक'+'ज़रा-सा' — महीने के अंत में बस ज़रा-सा बैलेंस।
examples: The family survived on an exiguous income after the factory closed.
Because of an exiguous harvest, the farmers had barely enough grain to last until the next season.

meaning: To officially clear someone of blame
trick: 'Ex'+'Honor' — पुराने कर्मचारी को स-सम्मान दोषों से बरी करना।
examples: The CCTV footage helped exonerate the bank manager from fraud charges.
The investigation helped exonerate the young cook, who had been blamed for the kitchen fire he did not start.

meaning: To speak or write at length on a subject
trick: 'Ex'+'Space' — बात को पूरी Space देकर फैलाना, यानी विस्तार से बोलना या लिखना।
examples: The finance minister expatiated on the benefits of the new tax reform.
The old guide would expatiate on every carving in the cave, sometimes talking for an hour about one statue.

meaning: To make an action happen faster
trick: 'Extra' + 'Speed' — Extra Speed लगाकर काम को जल्दी पूरा करना।
examples: The manager promised to expedite the loan approval process.
The courier agreed to expedite the parcel so that it would reach the bride's house before the wedding.

meaning: Done quickly and efficiently
trick: 'Expedite'+'ious' — जो काम को Expedite (तेज़) करे।
examples: The bank used expeditious methods to clear the customer's loan.
The rescue team was expeditious, reaching the flooded village within an hour and moving everyone to safety.

meaning: Still in existence
trick: 'Exist' — Extinct का मतलब विलुप्त और Extant का मतलब जो आज भी जीवित या मौजूद है।
examples: All banks must follow the extant guidelines issued by the RBI.
Only a handful of the ancient manuscripts are still extant, and most of them are kept in the museum.

meaning: To lessen the seriousness of a fault
trick: 'Extra'+'Tension'+'ghata' — मजबूरी बताकर अपराध या गलती की गंभीरता को कम करना।
examples: Even extreme poverty cannot extenuate the crime of bank robbery.
Nothing can extenuate the cruelty of leaving a helpless animal on the roadside in the burning heat.

meaning: To praise enthusiastically
trick: 'Extra'+'Tall' — जो एक्स्ट्रा ऊंचे दर्जे का काम करे उसकी सब प्रशंसा करते हैं।
examples: Financial experts extol the benefits of long- term investments.
The coach would extol the team's courage after every match, even when they had narrowly lost the game.

meaning: Irrelevant or unrelated to the subject
trick: 'Extra' — जो बात मुद्दे से बाहर और Extra (गैर-ज़रूरी) हो।
examples: Please remove all extraneous details from the final project report.
The editor deleted several extraneous paragraphs from the story because they had nothing to do with the plot.

meaning: Treating serious matters with inappropriate humor
trick: 'Face'+'Hasi' — गंभीर मीटिंग में भी चेहरे पर हँसी लाकर मज़ाकिया बात करना।
examples: The boss did not like his facetious remarks during the serious audit meeting.
The teacher frowned at the facetious boy who made silly jokes in the middle of the fire-safety drill.

meaning: Based on a mistaken belief
trick: 'False' — जो बात False हो वो गलत और भ्रामक होती है।
examples: The rumor about the bank going bankrupt was completely fallacious.
The belief that lightning never strikes the same place twice is fallacious, as tall towers are hit often.

meaning: A mistaken belief or false idea
trick: 'False'+'acy' — False (झूठी) बात।
examples: It is a fallacy that all debt is bad; some borrowing fuels growth.
It is a common fallacy that people use only ten percent of their brains, though science says otherwise.

meaning: To lose strength or momentum; to hesitate
trick: 'Fall' — चलते-चलते अचानक Fall होने लगना यानी लड़खड़ाना या कमजोर पड़ना।
examples: The economic recovery began to falter due to high inflation.
Her voice began to falter as she walked onto the stage and saw the huge crowd waiting for her.

meaning: A confused mixture; a hodgepodge
trick: 'Fair'+'Go' — मेले में सब चीज़ों का मिला-जुला ढेर।
examples: The report was a farrago of half-truths and unrelated statistics.
His school essay was a farrago of jokes, borrowed lines and random facts that never came together.

hindi: नखरेबाज़ / हर चीज़ में परफेक्शन चाहने वाला
meaning: Very attentive to detail; hard to please
trick: 'Fussy'+'Tidy' — Fussy (नखरेबाज़) + Tidy (साफ़-सुथरा) = हर चीज़ में Perfection चाहने वाला।
examples: Auditors are fastidious when checking the company's financial statements.
The fastidious tailor rechecked every stitch and refused to hand over the suit until each seam was perfect.

meaning: To understand after much thought
trick: 'Thah' — समुद्र की गहराई की थाह लेना यानी किसी गहरी बात को पूरी तरह समझना।
examples: It is hard to fathom why the company took such a huge financial risk.
Scientists still cannot fathom how some birds find their way across oceans without any maps or instruments.

meaning: Silly and pointless; foolish
trick: 'फ़ालतू' — फ़ालतू की बेवकूफ़ी भरी बातें करना, यानी मूर्खतापूर्ण।
examples: It was a fatuous decision to take a massive loan without a business plan.
The prince's fatuous speech about his own greatness made the wise old courtiers roll their eyes in silence.

meaning: Capable of producing a lot; fertile
trick: 'Fertile'+'कुंड' — Fertile ज़मीन जो फ़सलों का कुंड (भंडार) भर दे, यानी उपजाऊ।
examples: The Indian startup ecosystem is highly fecund for new innovations.
The fecund river valley gave three rich harvests a year and fed millions of people across the plains.

meaning: Well-chosen; apt and pleasing
trick: 'Fit'+'Delicious' — मौके पर बिलकुल Fit और सुनने में मीठी लगने वाली बात, यानी उचित।
examples: His felicitous remarks lightened the mood of the tense meeting.
A felicitous phrase from the host turned an awkward silence into laughter at the farewell dinner.

meaning: Intense passion or enthusiasm
trick: 'Fever' — देशभक्ति का फीवर चढ़ना मतलब जोश में आना।
examples: The scheme was promoted with great fervor across the country.
The fans cheered with fervor as their team ran onto the field for the final of the league.

meaning: A restraint; something that restricts freedom
trick: 'Feet'+'Tie' — Feet (पैरों) को Tie करके बाँधने वाली ज़ंजीर, यानी बेड़ी / बंधन।
examples: Excessive regulations can fetter the growth of small businesses.
Old customs can fetter young people, making it hard for them to choose their own careers or paths.

meaning: A complete failure, often humiliating
trick: 'फ़ीस'+'खो' — कोचिंग की पूरी फ़ीस खो दी और Result zero, यानी भारी विफलता।
examples: The product launch was a complete fiasco with zero customer interest.
The school play turned into a fiasco when the curtain fell on the lead actor and the lights failed.

meaning: Changing frequently; unreliable
trick: 'Fikar'+'Kal' — जिसे हर Kal (पल) Fikar (चिंता) बदल जाए वो चंचल मन है।
examples: Fickle market conditions make day trading very risky.
The fickle weather in the hills changes from bright sunshine to heavy rain within a single hour.

meaning: Faithfulness and loyalty
trick: 'Fi'+'दिल' — दिल सिर्फ़ एक के लिए, यानी वफ़ादारी।
examples: Fidelity to customer data privacy is a core value of the bank.
The loyal dog showed great fidelity, waiting at the station every evening for years after its master left.

meaning: Involving trust, especially with money
trick: 'FD'+'Bharosa' — आप बैंक में FD तभी कराते हैं जब बैंक आपका विश्वासपात्र होता है।
examples: A fund manager has a fiduciary duty to protect the investors' money.
As the trustee of the orphanage fund, he held a fiduciary responsibility to spend every rupee only on the children.

meaning: To steal something small
trick: 'फिसला' — दुकान से छोटी चीज़ चुपके से जेब में फिसला ली, यानी छोटी चोरी।
examples: The clerk was caught trying to filch cash from the till.
A hungry crow tried to filch a piece of bread from the picnic basket while the family was playing cricket.

meaning: Related to government revenue, taxes, and spending
trick: 'Fees'+'Tax' — सरकार की Tax-कमाई और खर्च का हिसाब।
examples: The finance minister presented the fiscal deficit report.
The government announced a fiscal plan to build more roads and schools without raising taxes this year.

meaning: Conspicuously offensive or bad
trick: 'Flag' — Flag (झंडा) लहराकर सबके सामने खुलेआम नियम तोड़ना, यानी घोर उल्लंंघन।
examples: The company was fined for its flagrant violation of tax laws.
The referee gave the player a red card for a flagrant foul that everybody in the stadium had seen.

meaning: Showy and elaborate in style
trick: 'Flame'+'ant' — Flame (आग) जैसी भड़कीली स्टाइल।
examples: The flamboyant businessman always arrived in the flashiest car.
The flamboyant dancer swept onto the stage in a bright red cape studded with shining sequins.

meaning: Excessively ornate or flushed
trick: 'Flower' — फूलों की तरह बहुत सजी हुई और भड़कीली चीज़।
examples: The manager's florid language could not hide the company's losses.
The old poet's florid style, full of long flowery phrases, tired readers who wanted a simple story.

meaning: To openly disregard a rule
trick: 'Foul'+'Out' — मैच में फाउल करके रेफरी के नियमों की अवज्ञा करना।
examples: Companies that flout environmental regulations will face heavy fines.
Drivers who flout traffic signals put pedestrians in danger and may lose their licences for months.

meaning: To stir up or incite trouble
trick: 'Foam'+'Mental' — लोगों का दिमाग भड़का कर दंगे या अशांति को हवा देना।
examples: Fake news on social media was used to foment panic among bank depositors.
Rumours spread by a few troublemakers can foment unrest and turn a peaceful town into a battlefield overnight.

meaning: Patient self-control; tolerance
trick: 'Bear' — मुसीबत में खुद पर काबू रखना और धैर्य दिखाना।
examples: The RBI announced regulatory forbearance to help small businesses during the crisis.
The teacher showed great forbearance, calmly repeating the lesson for the fifth time without raising her voice.

meaning: Pitifully sad and abandoned
trick: 'For'+'Loan' — लोन न चुका पाने के कारण आदमी अकेला और उदास महसूस कर रहा है।
examples: The abandoned office building looked completely forlorn.
The forlorn puppy sat in the rain outside the closed shop, waiting for someone to take him home.

meaning: Inspiring fear or respect through being large or powerful
trick: 'फ़ौजी'+'Able' — फ़ौजी जैसा ताकतवर Opponent, जिससे डर भी लगे और सम्मान भी।
examples: The bank faces a formidable challenge in recovering the bad loans.
The mountaineers faced a formidable wall of ice that rose almost straight up for hundreds of metres.

meaning: Courage in facing pain or adversity
trick: 'Fort'+'Attitude' — मुसीबत के समय किले जैसा मजबूत Attitude और साहस रखना।
examples: She bore the financial losses with great fortitude and rebuilt her business.
The nurses showed great fortitude, working through the night without rest during the deadly floods in the district.

meaning: Happening by chance, often lucky
trick: 'Fortune' — जो किस्मत या संयोग से अचानक मिल जाए।
examples: Meeting the angel investor on the train was a fortuitous event for his startup.
A fortuitous gust of wind blew the lost letter back to its owner just as she gave up the search.

meaning: A noisy disturbance or quarrel
trick: 'Fracture'+'Case' — झगड़ा, Fracture, फिर पुलिस Case।
examples: A fracas broke out between rival groups at the bank's annual meeting.
A fracas erupted at the market when two vendors began to shout about whose stall was too close to the road.

meaning: Irritable and quarrelsome
trick: 'Fracture' + 'ious' — जिसका मिजाज हर बात पर Fracture (टूट) जाए, यानी चिड़चिड़ा।
examples: The fractious crowd refused to listen to the security guards.
The fractious toddler kicked and screamed in the shop, refusing to hold his mother's hand or walk to the car.

meaning: Easily broken or damaged
trick: Parcel पर लिखा 'FRAGILE' — काँच का सामान, Handle with care, ज़रा-सा गिरा तो टूटा।
examples: The global supply chain is still fragile.
The fragile glass vase slipped from the shelf and shattered into a hundred pieces on the tiled floor.

meaning: Fast and energetic in a wild, uncontrolled way
trick: 'Free'+'Net' — Free WiFi मिलते ही सब पागलों की तरह ताबड़तोड़ Download करने लगे।
examples: There was frenetic buying on the stock exchange after the rate cut news.
The kitchen was a scene of frenetic activity as the cooks rushed to serve the wedding guests on time.

meaning: Not having any serious purpose or value
trick: 'Free'+'LOL' — Free time में बस LOL वाले Memes देखना, यानी तुच्छ और बेकार काम।
examples: The court dismissed the lawsuit, calling it completely frivolous.
The principal rejected the frivolous complaint of a student who wanted classes cancelled because it was too sunny.

meaning: Sparing with money; economical
trick: 'Free'+'Google' — जो पैसे बचाने के लिए हर चीज़ बस Free में Google पर ढूंढे वो मितव्ययी है।
examples: Living a frugal life in your twenties helps build a strong retirement fund.
The frugal widow mended her old clothes, grew her own vegetables and saved every coin for her grandchildren's school fees.

meaning: Tending to disappear; fleeting
trick: 'Fuse' (फ्यूज) + 'Gious' — फ्यूज होकर हवा में उड़ जाना, यानी जल्दी गायब होने वाला।
examples: The beauty of the cherry blossoms is fugacious, lasting only a few weeks.
The fugacious fragrance of jasmine flowers lingered in the evening air for a moment and was gone.

meaning: To protest strongly or criticize harshly
trick: 'Full'+'Minute' — Full Minute तक ज़ोरदार विरोध में बोलना।
examples: The union fulminated against the sudden salary deductions.
The villagers began to fulminate against the new factory that was poisoning their river with dark smoke and waste.

hindi: अति चापलूसी भरा / ज़रूरत से ज़्यादा
meaning: Excessive, especially of praise, to the point of being insincere
trick: 'Full'+'Some' — Full ज़्यादा होकर झूठी तारीफ हो जाना।
examples: The CEO received fulsome praise from his inner circle, which rang hollow.
The fulsome compliments of the salesman made the old lady suspicious, and she left the shop without buying anything.

meaning: Done secretly to avoid notice
trick: 'फ़ुर्र' — चिड़िया की तरह चुपके से फ़ुर्र हो जाना, यानी चोरी-छिपे।
examples: His furtive glances during the interview raised suspicion.
The cat gave a furtive glance around the kitchen before stealing the fish from the plate.

meaning: Rushing headlong, often to destruction
trick: 'गधा'+'Run' — गधों का झुंड बिना सोचे अंधाधुंध भागे, सीधा खाई की ओर।
examples: The Gadarene rush to invest in dubious schemes ended in disaster.
In a Gadarene panic, the crowd surged toward the narrow exit, trampling one another on the stairs.

meaning: An embarrassing blunder in public
trick: 'Gaffe' — छोटी सी गलती पर सबके सामने शर्मिंदगी।
examples: His gaffe at the board meeting made headlines in the business press.
The anchor's gaffe, calling the guest by the wrong name on live television, made the whole studio cringe.

hindi: इनकार करना / खंडन करना / विरोध करना
meaning: To deny or contradict a fact
trick: 'Against'+'Say' — किसी सच्ची बात के Against (खिलाफ) कुछ बोलना यानी इनकार करना।
examples: No one can gainsay the fact that UPI has revolutionized Indian banking.
No historian can gainsay that the ancient trade routes helped spread new ideas across Asia and Europe.

meaning: To shock or excite into taking action
trick: 'Galwan' — गलवान घटना ने पूरे देश को एकजुट होकर कुछ करने के लिए प्रेरित किया।
examples: The falling profits helped galvanize the management into taking bold steps.
The terrible floods helped galvanize the whole city, and thousands of volunteers arrived with food and boats.

meaning: A strategic move or opening sacrifice
trick: 'Game'+'Bit' — Game में एक चतुर चाल का Bit (हिस्सा)।
examples: The sudden tax cut was seen as a political gambit ahead of elections.
In chess, the young champion opened with a daring gambit, giving up a pawn to win the centre of the board.

meaning: To run or jump about playfully
trick: 'Gum'+'Ball' — रबड़ की उछलने वाली Gumball की तरह बच्चे उछल-कूद करते हैं।
examples: The children gambolled in the garden all afternoon.
The lambs gambolled across the green meadow in the spring sunshine while their mothers grazed quietly.

meaning: Extremely large in size or amount
trick: 'Ghar'+'Gainda' — घर जितना बड़ा गैंडा यानी विशाल।
examples: The company reported a gargantuan loss of ₹10,000 crore this quarter.
The gargantuan statue towered above the city square, and tourists had to step far back to see its face.

meaning: Excessively talkative
trick: 'Gali'+'Gali'+'Log' — गली-गली के Log (लोग) बहुत बातूनी होते हैं।
examples: He is so garrulous that meetings with him take twice as long.
The garrulous barber talked about politics, cricket and the weather without ever pausing to take a breath.

hindi: भद्दा / फूहड़ / सामाजिक रूप से अनाड़ी
meaning: Awkward and lacking social grace
trick: 'Oh Gosh!' — उसकी अनाड़ी और भद्दी हरकत देखकर सब बोले "Oh Gosh!"
examples: Talking loudly about your salary at a formal dinner is considered gauche.
The gauche young man tripped over the carpet and then spilled tea on the host's new sofa.

meaning: Extremely thin and bony, often from hunger or illness
trick: 'Gaanth' — इतना दुबला कि हड्डियों की गांठें दिखें।
examples: The gaunt beggar's eyes told a story of years of hunger.
After weeks without proper food, the gaunt traveller stumbled into the village, his cheeks hollow and his ribs showing.

meaning: Extremely cold or icy
trick: 'Jelly'+'id' — Jelly जैसा ठंडा और जमा हुआ।
examples: A gelid wind swept through the northern mountain villages.
The gelid waters of the glacial lake made the swimmers gasp and leave after only a few seconds.

hindi: सामान्य / बिना किसी विशेष ब्रांड का
meaning: Shared by a whole group; common
trick: 'General' — जेनेरिक दवाइयां किसी खास ब्रांड के नाम से नहीं बल्कि सामान्य नाम से मिलती हैं।
examples: The applicant gave a very generic answer instead of specific examples.
Many shops now sell generic medicines that cost far less than the famous brands but work just as well.

meaning: Relevant and appropriate to the subject
trick: 'Jad'+'Main' — जो बात मुद्दे की जड़ (Main Point) से जुड़ी हो यानी प्रासंगिक।
examples: The judge asked the lawyer to keep the arguments germane to the case.
The teacher asked the class to keep their comments germane to the poem and avoid talking about the weather.

meaning: To use gestures while speaking
trick: 'Gesture' — बात करते समय Gesture से इशारे करना।
examples: The orator gesticulated passionately while explaining the banking reforms.
The referee began to gesticulate wildly, waving his arms to tell the players that the goal did not count.

meaning: Fluent but insincere and shallow
trick: 'G'+'Lib' (Lip) — जिसकी Lip से बिना सोचे बातें निकलें।
examples: His glib answers failed to convince the interview panel.
The glib salesman had a ready smile and a quick answer for everything, but nobody really trusted him.

meaning: Excessively greedy in eating or consuming
trick: 'Gatagat' — गट-गट करके सब कुछ निगल जाने वाला यानी पेटू।
examples: His gluttonous appetite for acquisitions led the company into debt.
The gluttonous king demanded ten courses at every meal and grew too heavy to climb onto his own horse.

meaning: Extremely delicate and thin
trick: 'Go'+'Summer' — Summer की हल्की हवा में उड़ता पतला धागा।
examples: The gossamer fabric of the saree made it look almost weightless.
A gossamer veil of cobwebs, wet with morning dew, hung between the branches of the old garden hedge.

meaning: To swindle or overcharge someone
trick: 'Gaaj' — दुकानदार ने ऊँची कीमत की गाज ग्राहक पर गिरा दी यानी लूट लिया।
examples: The local vendors often try to gouge tourists during the peak season.
Some taxi drivers outside the station try to gouge visitors by demanding triple the proper fare for a short ride.

meaning: Using fancy words to impress; pompous
trick: 'Grand'+'Eloquent' — अपनी शान दिखाने के लिए बड़े- बड़े और भारी-भरकम शब्दों में बड़बोलापन दिखाना।
examples: Investors prefer clear numbers over grandiloquent promises from the CEO.
The mayor's grandiloquent speech, full of long words and empty phrases, left the farmers wondering what he had promised.

meaning: Excessively grand or ambitious
trick: 'Grand' (बड़ा) — Grand से भी ज़्यादा विशाल और दिखावटी सोच।
examples: The grandiose plans of the startup were never achieved on budget.
The king's grandiose dream of a golden city stretching from sea to sea was never even begun.

meaning: Uncalled for; done without good reason
trick: 'Grahak'+'Tu' — बिना किसी वजह के ग्राहक से तू-तड़ाक करना यानी अकारण।
examples: Avoid giving gratuitous advice to colleagues when they haven't asked for it.
The film was criticised for gratuitous violence that added nothing to the story and only shocked the audience.

meaning: Dignity, seriousness, or solemnity of manner
trick: 'Grave' (गंभीर) — जिसके चेहरे और आवाज़ में एक शानदार और गंभीर रुतबा हो।
examples: The RBI governor spoke with great gravitas during the press conference.
The elderly judge walked in with such gravitas that the noisy courtroom fell silent at once.

meaning: Fond of company; sociable
trick: 'Group' — जो इंसान Group में रहना पसंद करे।
examples: Sales jobs are best suited for people with a gregarious nature.
A gregarious child, he made friends on the very first day and invited the whole class to his birthday.

meaning: Sly or cunning intelligence
trick: 'Ghayal' — उसने अपनी धूर्त चालाकी और छल-कपट से सीधे-सादे ग्राहकों को ठग कर घायल कर दिया।
examples: The conman used charm and guile to trick people into the Ponzi scheme.
The fox in the folk tale used guile, pretending to be lame, to lure the hens out of their coop.

hindi: भोला / आसानी से धोखा खाने वाला
meaning: Easily deceived or tricked
trick: 'Gully'+'able' — Gully के बच्चे को आसानी से बहला लिया जाता है।
examples: Fraudsters target gullible senior citizens with fake investment schemes.
The gullible traveller believed the stranger's story about a sick child and handed over all his cash.

meaning: Overused and thus lacking originality
trick: 'Hack'+'Neend' — एक ही डायलॉग बार-बार सुनकर अब नींद आने लगी है क्योंकि वो बहुत घिसा-पिटा हो चुका है।
examples: Avoid using hackneyed phrases in your descriptive English essay.
The film was full of hackneyed lines that every viewer had heard in a hundred older movies.

meaning: Looking exhausted and unwell
trick: 'Hard'+'Guard' — रात भर जागे Guard का थका चेहरा।
examples: After the long audit, the manager looked pale and haggard.
After three sleepless nights at the hospital, the young father looked haggard, with dark circles under his tired eyes.

meaning: Peaceful and happy, especially of a past time
trick: 'Hello'+'Sun' — जब Hello (सुप्रभात) और Sun (सूरज) वाले सुखद शांतिपूर्णण दिन हों।
examples: Veteran bankers often recall the halcyon days of zero cyber fraud.
He often spoke fondly of the halcyon summers of his childhood, spent swimming in the village pond.

meaning: Made holy; greatly revered
trick: 'Hallow' = 'Holy' — शब्द में ही Holy (पवित्र) छुपा है यानी पवित्र।
examples: The hallowed halls of the central bank have seen many historic decisions.
Cricketers dream of playing on the hallowed turf of Lord's, where legends have walked for generations.

meaning: With no particular order or plan
trick: 'Half'+'Hazard' — आधा-अधूरा, जैसे-तैसे किया गया काम यानी बेतरतीब।
examples: A haphazard approach to investment can be very dangerous.
Books were piled in a haphazard heap in the corner, and finding the right one took ages.

meaning: Unlucky and unfortunate
trick: 'Helpless' — जो बेचारा Helpless (असहाय) हो वही अभागा होता है।
examples: The hapless customers lost their life savings in the chit-fund scam.
The hapless tourists missed their train, lost their luggage and then got caught in a sudden downpour.

meaning: A lengthy and aggressive speech
trick: 'Har'+'Ang' — गुस्से में हर अंग हिला-हिलाकर लंबा और ज़ोरदार भाषण देना।
examples: The manager delivered a lengthy harangue about discipline and punctuality.
The angry coach delivered a long harangue to the losing team, shouting about laziness for almost an hour.

meaning: A sign of something coming in the future
trick: 'Har'+'Finger' — हर उंगली से इशारा करके आगे आने वाले खतरे का संकेत देना।
examples: The sudden drop in manufacturing output was a harbinger of recession.
The first swallows of the season are a harbinger of spring, bringing hope after the long cold winter.

meaning: A strict, irritable old woman
trick: 'Har'+'Din' — जो बुढ़िया हर दिन सबसे झगड़ा करे।
examples: The harridan next door complained about every small noise.
The children avoided the old harridan on the corner, who scolded anyone that dared to step on her lawn.

meaning: Arrogantly superior and disdainful
trick: 'Hot' — जो खुद को बहुत Hot समझे वो घमंडी हो जाता है।
examples: His haughty attitude makes him very unpopular among his colleagues.
The haughty princess looked down on the servants and never thanked them for anything they did for her.

meaning: Favoring aggressive or strict policies (esp. on interest rates)
trick: 'Hawk' — बाज की नज़र सख्त रवैये वाली होती है।
examples: The RBI maintained a hawkish stance to control inflation.
The coach took a hawkish line against late arrivals, announcing that anyone who was late would be dropped from the squad.

meaning: To bully or intimidate someone
trick: 'Hekdi' — हेकड़ी दिखाकर किसी को डराना-धमकाना।
examples: The senior manager tried to hector the new recruits into working overtime.
The bossy older boy tried to hector the younger children into carrying his bag all the way to school.

meaning: Protected against risk, especially financially
trick: 'Hedge' — जैसे खेत के चारों तरफ बाड़ लगाकर फसल सुरक्षित करते हैं वैसे नुकसान से बचने के लिए निवेश सुरक्षित करना।
examples: The company hedged its foreign currency exposure to avoid losses from rupee falls.
The farmer hedged against a poor monsoon by selling part of his crop early at a fixed price.

meaning: A person devoted to pleasure
trick: 'Head'+'On' — जिसका Head सिर्फ भोग-विलास में On रहे।
examples: The billionaire lived the life of a hedonist, traveling the world on a yacht.
The prince, a true hedonist, spent every night at feasts and never once attended a council meeting.

meaning: Dominance of one group over others
trick: 'Huge'+'Money' — जिसके पास Huge Money हो उसका दबदबा होता है।
examples: The dollar maintains its hegemony in international trade.
For centuries, one powerful empire held hegemony over the region, and smaller kingdoms had to pay tribute to it.

meaning: Utterly wicked or evil
trick: 'Hinsa' — बहुत ही घिनौनी हिंसा और जघन्य अपराध।
examples: Stealing pension funds of poor widows is a heinous financial crime.
The villagers were stunned by the heinous crime and demanded that the guilty be punished at once.

meaning: A figure of speech using two words connected by 'and' to express one idea
trick: 'Di' (दो) + 'Idea' — दो शब्द, एक Idea; जैसे 'nice and warm' = 'nicely warm'।
examples: Using 'cup and gold' instead of 'golden cup' is an example of hendiadys.
In grammar class we learned that the phrase sound and fury is a case of hendiadys, expressing one idea with two nouns.

meaning: A belief or opinion contrary to orthodox religious doctrine
trick: 'Haira'+'See' — ऐसी बात जिसे सुनकर धर्मगुरु हैरान रह जाएं क्योंकि वो धर्म के खिलाफ है।
examples: In some strict societies, questioning old traditions is considered heresy.
In medieval Europe, teaching that the earth moved around the sun was branded heresy and could land you in prison.

hindi: विधर्मी / परंपरा के खिलाफ जाने वाला
meaning: A person holding a belief contrary to established doctrine
trick: 'Heresy'+'Critic' — Heresy (धर्म-विरोधी बात) करने वाला Critic यानी विधर्मी व्यक्ति।
examples: Anyone who opposed the ancient customs was considered a heretic.
The scientist was branded a heretic by the church for claiming that the stars were distant suns.

hindi: पूरी तरह बंद / वायुरुद्ध / बाहरी प्रभाव से अछूता
meaning: Completely sealed; airtight
trick: 'Har'+'Matka' — हर मटके का मुँह इतना टाइट बंद कि हवा भी अंदर न जा सके।
examples: No economy can remain hermetic in today's interconnected global market.
The astronaut checked that the hermetic seal on the capsule door was tight before the rocket lifted off.

meaning: Diverse in character or content
trick: 'Hetero' = 'Hatke' — हटके यानी अलग-अलग तरह के लोगों का मेल।
examples: India has a heterogeneous banking customer base across states.
The festival drew a heterogeneous crowd of farmers, students, tourists and traders, all dressed in different styles.

meaning: A pause or gap in a sequence
trick: 'Hata'+'Us' — काम से कुछ समय के लिए हट जाना यानी बीच में एक छोटा सा ब्रेक या ठहराव लेना।
examples: After a two-year hiatus, the company resumed its hiring process.
After a long hiatus, the famous rock band returned to the stage and played to a packed stadium.

meaning: To create difficulties that delay progress
trick: 'Behind' — पीछे से खींचकर रोकना यानी रुकावट डालना।
examples: Poor internet connectivity can hinder digital banking in villages.
Thick fog can hinder the rescue helicopters, which are unable to fly safely over the mountain range.

meaning: Hairy or shaggy
trick: 'Hair'+'suit' — जिसके शरीर पर Hair का Suit हो।
examples: The hirsute traveller in the jungle survived on wild fruits.
The hirsute wrestler had thick dark hair on his arms and chest and a beard that reached his belt.

meaning: Overly theatrical or dramatic
trick: 'Hi'+'Theatre-On' — 'Hi' बोलते ही जिसका Theatre (नाटक) On हो जाए यानी नाटकीय।
examples: Her histrionic reaction to a minor error surprised everyone.
The toddler's histrionic crying, with dramatic gasps and flailing arms, ended the moment he was offered an ice cream.

hindi: समान / एक ही प्रकार का / समरूप
meaning: Of the same kind; uniform in nature
trick: 'Homo' = 'Home' — एक ही घर (Home) के सब लोग एक जैसे यानी समान।
examples: Rural markets are not homogeneous; every village has different banking needs.
The class was far from homogeneous, with pupils of many languages, customs and levels of ability learning side by side.

meaning: Excessive pride or self-confidence
trick: 'Hub' — जो खुद को दुनिया का Hub (केंद्र) माने उसमें घमंड आ गया।
examples: His hubris prevented him from taking advice from senior managers.
The champion's hubris led him to skip practice, and he was beaten in the first round by a newcomer.

meaning: Exaggerated statements not meant literally
trick: 'Hyper'+'Boli' — किसी बात को ज़रूरत से ज़्यादा Hyper होकर बढ़ा-चढ़ाकर बोलना।
examples: Saying that AI will replace all bankers tomorrow is pure hyperbole.
Calling the small bakery the best in the universe was hyperbole, but the cakes were truly good.

meaning: Over-ambitious or recklessly adventurous
trick: 'I'+'Car' — बिना ब्रेक की Car दौड़ाना यानी अति साहस।
examples: The Icarian investment scheme collapsed within a year.
The Icarian plan to build a tower to the clouds with no strong foundation fell apart before the second floor.

meaning: The study of fish
trick: 'Ik-Thi'+'logy' — "इक थी मछली…" का अध्ययन।
examples: Ichthyology is crucial for understanding marine ecosystems.
Our teacher, who studies ichthyology, can identify nearly every fish in the river just by looking at its fins.

meaning: A person who attacks cherished beliefs or traditions
trick: 'Icon'+'Clash' — जो पुरानी Icons से Clash करे और उन्हें तोड़ दे।
examples: The new governor is an iconoclast who changed decades-old banking rules.
The young painter, a true iconoclast, mocked the old masters and displayed her art on the street instead of in galleries.

meaning: A distinctive or peculiar habit
trick: 'Idiot'+'Sing'+'Crazy' — हर Idiot की अपनी एक अलग तरह की Sing (आवाज़) और Crazy आदत होती है।
examples: His idiosyncrasy of reading every file twice amused his colleagues.
One idiosyncrasy of the old professor was that he always wore mismatched socks and carried an umbrella even in summer.

meaning: Extremely peaceful and picturesque
trick: 'Ideal'+'ic' — Ideal (आदर्श) गाँव की शांत ज़िंदगी।
examples: The idyllic countryside surroundings made the banker forget city stress.
The tiny cottage by the lake, surrounded by green hills, looked so idyllic that visitors never wanted to leave.

meaning: Not honorable in character or purpose
trick: 'In' (नहीं) + 'Noble' (महान) — जो Noble न हो बल्कि घटिया हो।
examples: It was an ignoble act to blame the junior clerk for one's own error.
Stealing a poor man's lunch is an ignoble deed, and the boy was ashamed of himself afterward.

meaning: Deserving or causing public disgrace
trick: 'Ig'+'Nomin' (No Name) — नाम (इज़्ज़त) मिट्टी में मिल जाए, ऐसा शर्मनाक।
examples: The team suffered an ignominious defeat in the final match.
After the ignominious loss, the captain had to walk off the field while the crowd booed loudly.

meaning: Deep personal humiliation and disgrace
trick: 'Ig'+'Nomin' (No Name) — नाम (इज़्ज़त) मिट्टी में मिल जाना यानी बदनामी।
examples: The bank's chairman resigned in ignominy after the fraud was exposed.
The disgraced minister lived the rest of his life in ignominy, shunned by old friends and neighbours.

meaning: Forbidden by law or rules
trick: 'Illegal'+'it' — Illegal (गैर-कानूनी) चीज़।
examples: The RBI is cracking down on illicit money transfers through shell companies.
Police raided the warehouse and seized crates of illicit goods that had been smuggled across the border at night.

meaning: A confused or complicated situation
trick: 'I'm'+'Bro'+'Glue' — मैं और Bro Glue से चिपक गए, अब छूट ही नहीं पा रहे यानी उलझन।
examples: The merger turned into a legal imbroglio involving three regulators.
The simple property dispute grew into a tangled imbroglio, with five relatives claiming the same plot of land.

hindi: भावना से भर देना / रंग देना
meaning: To inspire or permeate with a feeling or quality
trick: 'In'+'Blue' — कपड़े को Blue रंग में डुबोकर पूरा रंग देना, वैसे ही मन को भावना से भर देना।
examples: Good teachers imbue students with curiosity and confidence.
The coach tried to imbue his young players with a love of fair play as well as the will to win.

hindi: कैद करना / दीवारों में बंद करना
meaning: To enclose or imprison within walls
trick: 'In'+'Mayur' — मोर (मयूर) को दीवारों के अंदर कैद कर दिया।
examples: The witness was virtually immured in a safe house until the trial.
In the old story, the cruel king would immure his enemies in a tower and forget about them forever.

meaning: Unchanging over time; unchangeable
trick: 'Im' (नहीं) + 'Mutate' — जो वायरस की तरह कभी Mutate न हो यानी कभी न बदले।
examples: Blockchain technology creates an immutable record of financial transactions.
The laws of the old kingdom were thought to be immutable, but the new ruler changed them within a year.

meaning: To weaken or damage
trick: 'In'+'Pair' — पैर में चोट लग जाए तो चलने की क्षमता कमजोर हो जाती है।
examples: Rising bad loans can severely impair a bank's lending capacity.
Loud music for many years can impair your hearing and leave you unable to follow a quiet conversation.

meaning: Without fault or error; perfect
trick: 'Im'+'Pakka' — जिसका काम इतना पक्का और परफेक्ट हो कि उसमें कोई गलती न निकाल सके।
examples: You need an impeccable credit score to get the lowest interest rate.
The pianist's timing was impeccable, and not a single note was out of place during the two-hour concert.

meaning: Having little or no money
trick: 'Im'+'Pe'+'Cu' — "न पैसा, न कुछ" यानी कंगाल।
examples: The impecunious student worked part-time to fund his coaching classes.
The impecunious poet lived in a tiny rented room and often skipped dinner because he could not afford it.

meaning: To delay or block progress
trick: 'Im'+'Ped' (पेड़) — पेड़ गिराकर रास्ता रोकना।
examples: Poor infrastructure can impede the growth of digital banking.
Fallen trees and rocks can impede traffic on the mountain road after a heavy storm.

meaning: Something that slows down or blocks progress
trick: 'Im'+'Ped' (पेड़) — रास्ते में गिरा पेड़ यानी बाधा।
examples: High inflation is a major impediment to economic growth.
A stammer was no impediment to the boy, who went on to become a fine speaker and teacher.

meaning: To drive or force someone to action
trick: 'I am'+'Compel' — मैं Compel (मजबूर) हूँ इसलिए कुछ करने को प्रेरित हूँ।
examples: The need for financial inclusion impelled the RBI to launch Jan Dhan Yojana.
Hunger impelled the young man to leave his village and look for work in the city.

meaning: Arrogantly domineering or overbearing
trick: 'I am' + 'Superior' — जो अपने आप को सबसे सुपीरियर और बॉस माने।
examples: The imperious manager refused to listen to any employee suggestions.
The imperious queen waved away her ministers' advice and ordered the palace gates closed without listening to anyone.

meaning: Rude and not showing proper respect
trick: 'Important' नहीं — जो बड़ों को Important न समझे और उनसे ढीठ होकर बदतमीज़ी से बात करे।
examples: The interviewer was annoyed by the candidate's impertinent reply.
The teacher scolded the impertinent boy who laughed at her accent and mimicked her in front of the class.

meaning: Acting quickly without thought
trick: 'Impatient' — बेसब्र (Impatient) आदमी बिना सोचे-समझे जल्दबाज़ी करता है।
examples: The impetuous decision to take a massive loan ruined his finances.
In an impetuous moment, she jumped into the river to save her hat and had to be rescued herself.

meaning: Implied though not directly stated
trick: 'Im' = 'In' (अंदर) — बात अंदर छुपी है यानी निहित। (Explicit: Ex = Exit, बात बाहर खुलकर)
examples: Silence is often taken as implicit agreement in board meetings.
There was an implicit warning in his calm voice, and everyone in the room understood that he meant business.

hindi: अंदर की ओर धंसना / अचानक ढह जाना
meaning: To collapse inward violently
trick: 'Explode' का उल्टा — Explode मतलब बाहर फटना और Implode मतलब अंदर ही अंदर धंस जाना।
examples: Heavy debt caused the real estate bubble to implode overnight.
The old stadium was brought down in seconds, as the whole structure seemed to implode in a cloud of dust.

meaning: A curse
trick: 'Im'+'Preca' (प्रकोप) — प्रकोप (क्रोध) में दी गई बद्दुआ यानी शाप।
examples: In anger, the old man muttered imprecations against his enemies.
The defeated general walked away muttering imprecations at the weather, at his soldiers and at the god of war.

meaning: Done without being planned or rehearsed
trick: 'Prompt'+'Tu' — अचानक (Prompt) कहा गया "चल तू बोल!" यानी बिना तैयारी के।
examples: The singer gave an impromptu performance at the local cafe.
The rain stopped suddenly, and the neighbours held an impromptu party in the street with whatever food they had.

meaning: To attack as false or questionable
trick: 'Impure' — किसी की ईमानदारी को Impure बताकर उस पर सवाल उठाना।
examples: No one dared to impugn the integrity of the RBI governor.
No one in the town dared to impugn the honesty of the old judge, who had served for forty years.

meaning: To attribute blame or responsibility
trick: 'In'+'Put' — किसी के सिर पर गलती Put (डाल) देना यानी आरोप लगाना।
examples: The company imputed the financial losses to rising raw material costs.
The teacher refused to impute bad intentions to the boy, since he had only broken the window by accident.

meaning: Not resulting from deliberate planning; accidental
trick: 'In'+'Attention' नहीं — ध्यान न होने की वजह से जो गलती अनजाने में हो जाए।
examples: An inadvertent typing error transferred ten lakhs instead of ten thousand.
An inadvertent click on the wrong button deleted the whole album of holiday photographs from my phone.

meaning: Continuing without pause
trick: 'In'+'Cease' — कभी Ceasefire न हो यानी लगातार।
examples: The incessant noise from the construction site disturbed the bank's customers.
The incessant barking of the neighbour's dog kept us awake all night and gave me a headache the next day.

meaning: Just begun; not fully formed
trick: 'In'+'Chhote' — अभी ये प्लान बहुत छोटे (शुरुआती) स्तर पर है।
examples: The startup's business model is still in an inchoate stage.
The inchoate plan was little more than a few sketches on a napkin, and nobody knew how it would work.

meaning: Penetratingly clear and direct
trick: 'In'+'Scissor' — कैंची (Scissor) जैसा तेज़ और सटीक विश्लेषण।
examples: The newspaper published an incisive analysis of the annual budget.
The incisive question from the young reporter cut straight to the heart of the matter and left the minister speechless.

hindi: निर्विवाद / अकाट्य (जिसे झुठलाया न जा सके)
meaning: Impossible to deny or dispute
trick: 'In'+'Controversy' — जिस सबूत पर कोई Controversy (विवाद) हो ही न सके यानी निर्विवाद सत्य।
examples: The investigators presented incontrovertible proof of the digital fraud.
The detective found incontrovertible proof of the theft, a clear photograph showing the thief climbing out of the window.

meaning: To instill an idea or habit by persistent instruction
trick: 'In'+'Kul' — कुल (परिवार) के संस्कार मन में बैठाना।
examples: Parents must inculcate the habit of saving money in children early.
Good schools try to inculcate honesty and respect in their pupils through daily example and the stories they tell.

meaning: Currently holding an office or position
trick: 'In'+'Cabin' — जो अभी Cabin के अंदर बैठा है यानी वर्तमान पदधारी।
examples: The incumbent chairman was re-elected for another term.
The incumbent mayor promised to finish the new bridge if the people chose him for another term.

meaning: Tireless; never showing fatigue
trick: 'India'+'Defeat'+'Fatigue' — India को कोई Defeat नहीं कर सकता और Fatigue भी नहीं आती।
examples: The indefatigable team worked all night to finish the bank audit.
The indefatigable mountain guide led the group up the steep trail for ten hours without once asking for rest.

meaning: Native to a particular place
trick: 'Indi'+'Gen' — जो इंडिया में ही पैदा हुआ या बना हो, स्वदेशी।
examples: The government is promoting indigenous technology in the banking sector.
Cedar trees and tigers are indigenous to these forests, and no one introduced them from any other land.

meaning: Extremely poor; needy
trick: 'Indi'+'Tang' (तंगहाल) — जिसकी जेब हमेशा तंग रहे और जो बेहद गरीब व ज़रूरतमंद हो।
examples: Microfinance institutions provide small loans to indigent families.
The kind doctor ran a free clinic for indigent patients who could not pay even for a simple medicine.

meaning: Habitually lazy; avoiding activity
trick: 'In'+'Dole' — जो अपनी जगह से हिले-डुले भी नहीं वो आलसी।
examples: An indolent employee cannot survive in the fast-paced corporate world.
The indolent cat spent the whole day stretched on the warm window ledge and ignored the mice completely.

meaning: Impossible to defeat or subdue
trick: 'In'+'Dominate' — जिसे कोई Dominate न कर सके।
examples: Her indomitable spirit helped her rebuild the business after the crash.
Despite repeated failures, the explorer's indomitable will pushed him onward until he reached the unmapped island.

hindi: अवर्णनीय (शब्दों में न कहा जा सके)
meaning: Too great to be described in words
trick: 'In'+'Fable' — जिसे Fable (कहानी) में भी बयान न किया जा सके।
examples: Clearing the final exam brought him ineffable joy.
The beauty of the sunrise over the snowy peaks was ineffable, and no words could capture how it felt.

hindi: अनिवार्य / अपरिहार्य (जिससे बचा न जा सके)
meaning: Unable to be avoided or escaped
trick: 'In'+'Luck'+'Taal' — किस्मत के लिखे को कोई टाल नहीं सकता वह अनिवार्य है।
examples: Digital transformation is an ineluctable reality for modern banks.
Growing old is an ineluctable part of life, and no medicine or magic can stop it for anyone.

meaning: Having no skill; clumsy
trick: 'In'+'Expert' — जो अपने काम में बिल्कुल भी Expert न हो यानी अकुशल और अनाड़ी।
examples: The company suffered losses due to inept financial management.
The inept waiter dropped the tray twice, mixed up the orders and then poured soup into a customer's lap.

hindi: अटल / जिसे रोका न जा सके / निर्मम
meaning: Impossible to stop or change
trick: 'In'+'Roka' — समय की रफ़्तार या महंगाई जो बिना रुके लगातार बढ़ती ही जाए।
examples: The inexorable rise in automation is changing the nature of banking jobs.
The inexorable flood waters rose through the night, covering the fields and finally entering the sleeping village.

meaning: Extremely small; tiny
trick: 'Infinite'+'Small' — डेसीमल के बाद अनंत ज़ीरो लगा दो तो संख्या बहुत ही सूक्ष्म हो जाती है।
examples: The chances of a security breach in this encrypted system are infinitesimal.
The difference in height between the twin brothers was infinitesimal, a fraction of a millimetre at most.

meaning: Expanded or increased beyond normal
trick: 'In'+'Flat' — Flat टायर में हवा In (अंदर) भरी तो वो फूलकर बढ़ गया।
examples: Inflated property prices make housing unaffordable for many.
The shopkeeper's inflated claims about his sweets did not match the bland taste of the stale laddoos.

meaning: A general rise in prices; decrease in money's value
trick: 'Inflate' (फूलना) — गुब्बारे की तरह पैसों की कीमत कम होना और चीज़ों के दाम फूलना।
examples: High food prices are the primary driver of retail inflation this month.
Grandmother often complains that inflation has made it difficult to buy even a basket of vegetables with a small note.

hindi: मन में जगह बनाना / खुश करना
meaning: To bring oneself into favor by deliberate effort
trick: 'In'+'Great'+'Ji' — बॉस को बार-बार "Great जी!" बोलकर उसके मन में जगह बनाना।
examples: He tried to ingratiate himself with the new branch manager by doing small favors.
The new student tried to ingratiate himself with the teacher by praising her lessons and carrying her books daily.

meaning: Existing as a natural, permanent part of something
trick: 'In' (अंदर) + 'Here' (यहाँ) — जो गुण जन्म से आपके अंदर ही मौजूद हो।
examples: Volatility is an inherent feature of the equity market.
Danger is inherent in mountaineering, and even the most careful climbers must accept that weather can turn deadly.

meaning: Tending to harm or obstruct
trick: 'Enemy'+'Kal' — Enemy हमेशा आपके लिए हानिकारक होता है।
examples: High inflation is inimical to steady economic growth.
Constant noise and dust are inimical to the health of the patients living near the highway.

meaning: Not harmful or offensive
trick: 'Innocent' — जो चीज़ बिल्कुल मासूम और सीधी-सादी हो जिससे किसी को नुकसान न पहुँचे।
examples: He made an innocuous joke to break the ice during the meeting.
Though the dog barked loudly at the gate, it was innocuous and only wanted a biscuit from the visitors.

hindi: अतृप्त / जिसे कभी संतुष्ट न किया जा सके
meaning: Impossible to satisfy
trick: 'In'+'Satisfy' — जिसे कभी Satisfy (संतुष्ट) न किया जा सके वो अतृप्त है।
examples: The CEO had an insatiable appetite for acquiring smaller fintech startups.
The boy's insatiable curiosity led him to take apart every clock in the house to see how it worked.

hindi: कपटी / चुपचाप नुकसान पहुँचाने वाला / घातक
meaning: Proceeding in a gradual, subtle way but with harmful effects
trick: 'Inside' (अंदर ही अंदर) — दीमक या धीमे ज़हर की तरह जो अंदर ही अंदर चुपचाप भारी नुकसान पहुँचाए।
examples: Inflation is an insidious tax that slowly eats away your savings.
The insidious fog crept silently over the harbour and the sailors realised too late that they had lost their way.

meaning: Lacking flavor, interest, or excitement
trick: 'In'+'Sip' — चाय की एक Sip (घूंट) लेते ही पता चल गया चाय फीकी है।
examples: The company's new advertisement campaign was dull and insipid.
The insipid soup had no salt or spice, and the guests politely pushed their bowls away after one spoonful.

meaning: Rude and disrespectful
trick: 'Insult' — जो बात-बात पर बड़ों की Insult करे वो ढीठ है।
examples: The clerk was suspended for his insolent behavior toward the manager.
The insolent boy answered the old priest with a sneer, and his father made him apologise at once.

meaning: Unable to pay debts
trick: 'In'+'Solve'+'Rent' — जो अपना Rent और Loan Solve न कर सके वो दिवालिया है।
examples: The bank seized the assets of the insolvent borrower.
After years of poor harvests, the insolvent farmer had to sell his land to pay what he owed the moneylender.

meaning: Showing a casual lack of concern
trick: 'In'+'Sochi' — जिसने कुछ Sochi ही नहीं, वो बेफिक्र।
examples: His insouciant attitude toward the deadline annoyed his team.
The insouciant tourist strolled past the storm warning sign, humming a tune as if nothing could go wrong.

meaning: Narrow-minded; isolated from outside influence
trick: 'Insulation' — जो अपने दिमाग के चारों तरफ परत चढ़ा ले और बाहरी दुनिया के नए विचारों को न अपनाए।
examples: Companies with an insular mindset often fail in global markets.
Living in an insular village for decades, the elders distrusted anything that came from beyond the hills.

meaning: A person who takes part in a dialogue or conversation
trick: 'Inter'+'Lok'+'Talk' — बातचीत के बीच (Inter) बैठे लोग (Lok) जो Talk करें, वो वार्ताकार।
examples: The interviewer was a tough interlocutor, asking very tricky questions.
During the radio show, the host proved a patient interlocutor who let the guest finish every thought.

meaning: Occurring at irregular intervals; not continuous
trick: 'Interval'+'Minute' — फिल्म के Interval की तरह जो काम लगातार न होकर रुक-रुक कर हो।
examples: Intermittent server downtime caused trouble for UPI users today.
Intermittent showers through the afternoon forced the cricket umpires to stop play several times.

meaning: Hard to control or solve
trick: 'In'+'Track' — जिस समस्या या ज़िद्दी इंसान को वापस सही Track (रास्ते) पर लाना बहुत मुश्किल हो।
examples: Unemployment remains an intractable problem for many developing economies.
Doctors admitted that the patient's intractable cough had resisted every treatment they had tried.

hindi: ज़िद्दी / अड़ियल / समझौता न करने वाला
meaning: Refusing to compromise or change one's views
trick: 'In'+'Tass-se-Mass'+'Gent' — ऐसा Gent जो अपनी बात से टस-से-मस न हो और कोई समझौता न करे।
examples: Talks failed because the union leaders remained intransigent on their demands.
The intransigent neighbour refused to move his fence an inch, even after the court gave its verdict.

meaning: Fearless; adventurous
trick: 'In'+'Trap' — जो मुसीबत के Trap (जाल) में फँसकर भी न डरे वो निडर है।
examples: Intrepid entrepreneurs often invest in unexplored markets.
The intrepid explorer crossed the frozen river alone to reach the stranded villagers.

hindi: बाढ़ ला देना / ढेर लगा देना / भर देना
meaning: To overwhelm with too much of something
trick: 'In'+'Under'+'Water' — In (अंदर) सब Under (नीचे) पानी के, यानी बाढ़ या भरमार।
examples: The bank helpline was inundated with calls after the server crashed.
Teachers were inundated with assignments to grade just before the winter holidays began.

meaning: Insulting, abusive language
trick: 'In'+'Bakte' — गुस्से में किसी को उल्टा-सीधा बकना और गाली-गलौज या अपमानजनक भाषा बोलना।
examples: A professional debate should rely on facts, not personal invective.
The coach hurled invective at the referee, and the league later fined him for his language.

meaning: To persuade someone through deception
trick: 'In'+'Vehicle' — Vehicle में बिठाकर बहला-फुसलाकर ले जाना।
examples: The conman inveigled the senior citizen into signing over his property.
The salesman tried to inveigle the old woman into buying a costly water purifier she did not need.

meaning: Long-established and unlikely to change
trick: 'In'+'Veteran' — जो किसी आदत में पुराना Veteran (अनुभवी) हो चुका हो।
examples: Never lend money to an inveterate gambler.
He is an inveterate liar who cannot answer even a simple question truthfully.

meaning: Easily angered
trick: 'I'+'Rash' — Rash driver की तरह छोटी-सी बात पर भड़क जाने वाला गुस्सैल इंसान।
examples: It is hard to work under an irascible boss.
The irascible old chef threw spoons around the kitchen whenever an order came out late.

meaning: Aiming or promoting peace
trick: 'I'+'Rain' — Rain के बाद सब शांत, यानी शांतिप्रिय।
examples: The bank took an irenic approach to resolving the dispute with the union.
The elders adopted an irenic tone, hoping to end the long feud between the two families.

hindi: अटल / अपरिवर्तनीय (जिसे रद्द न किया जा सके)
meaning: Not able to be changed or reversed
trick: 'Ir'+'Revoke' — ऐसा फैसला जिसे एक बार जारी करने के बाद वापस न लिया जा सके।
examples: The exporter demanded an irrevocable letter of credit from the buyer's bank.
Once the court issued its irrevocable order, neither side could ask for the decision to be altered.

meaning: An impudent or conceited person
trick: 'Jack'+'Ape' — Jack नाम का लड़का जो Ape (बंदर) की तरह उछल-कूद और अकड़ दिखाए।
examples: The young jackanapes in the office thought he could run the bank better than the CEO.
The conceited jackanapes strutted through the party, boasting loudly and mocking the older guests.

meaning: Boasting or bragging
trick: 'Jack'+'Station' — Station पर खड़े Jack की डींगें।
examples: The politician's jactation about his achievements bored the audience.
The cricketer's endless jactation about his records irritated his teammates more than any defeat.

meaning: To fling or toss about
trick: 'Jack'+'Titli' — Jack तितली (Titli) पकड़ने के लिए हाथ इधर-उधर उछालता है।
examples: The boxer jactitated his gloves before the match began.
In his sleep the fevered patient began to jactitate in bed, tossing the blankets about restlessly.

meaning: The act of boasting or bragging
trick: 'Jack'+'Station' — Jack रेलवे Station पर खड़ा होकर सबको अपनी शेखी सुनाता है।
examples: His constant jactitation about his wealth made him very unpopular.
Humble people avoid jactitation, letting their quiet work speak for them.

meaning: Tired, bored, or lacking enthusiasm
trick: 'Ja'+'Dead' — "जा, मैं तो Dead हूँ!" — इतना थका हुआ।
examples: After years of routine work, the clerk felt jaded with his job.
The jaded traveller had seen so many palaces that even the Taj Mahal barely impressed him.

meaning: Having a cynical or bitter outlook
trick: 'Jaundice' — पीलिया (Jaundice) जैसी पीली और कड़वी नज़र।
examples: A jaundiced view of competitors often blinds a company to its own flaws.
Having been cheated twice, she took a jaundiced view of every offer that sounded too good.

meaning: Dull and lacking substance
trick: 'Je'+'Junior' — Junior बच्चे जैसी बचकानी और फीकी (नीरस) बात।
examples: The jejune arguments of the speaker failed to impress the board.
The film was so jejune that half the audience left before the interval.

meaning: To put something in danger of harm or failure
trick: 'Jaan'+'Par'+'Die' — ऐसा काम जिससे जान पर बन आए और Die होने का खतरा हो।
examples: Ignoring KYC norms can jeopardize the bank's licence.
Reckless driving can jeopardize the lives of passengers and pedestrians alike.

hindi: फेंक देना / त्याग देना (बोझ कम करने के लिए)
meaning: To throw off or discard something unnecessary
trick: 'Jet' — जब Jet प्लेन खतरे में हो तो उसे हल्का करने के लिए फालतू सामान नीचे फेंक दिया जाता है।
examples: The company decided to jettison its loss-making branches to save costs.
The pilot had to jettison extra fuel before attempting the emergency landing.

meaning: Extreme, aggressive patriotism
trick: 'Jingle'+'ism' — Jingle की तरह चिल्लाकर देशभक्ति का झूठा दिखावा।
examples: Economic jingoism can harm trade relations between countries.
Newspapers fanned jingoism before the war, urging citizens to hate the neighbouring country.

meaning: Cheerful and good-humored
trick: 'Joke' — जो इंसान हर वक्त Joke मारता रहे और माहौल को मज़ाकिया बनाए रखे।
examples: The manager's jocular nature kept the branch staff stress-free.
Her jocular remarks about the rainy weather made the tired hikers laugh.

meaning: To push or bump roughly
trick: 'Josh'+'Hustle' — मेट्रो में चढ़ने के Josh में Hustle करना, यानी धक्का-मुक्की।
examples: The eager fans jostled each other to get a glimpse of the celebrity.
Commuters jostle one another on the railway platform during the evening rush.

meaning: Cheerful and friendly
trick: 'Jovial' = 'Jolly' — दोनों J से शुरू, दोनों का मतलब हँसमुख और खुशमिज़ाज।
examples: The jovial branch manager kept the atmosphere light even under pressure.
Our jovial uncle arrived with sweets and funny stories, lifting everyone's mood at the wedding.

meaning: Extremely happy and joyful, especially after a success
trick: 'Jubilee' — जब कंपनी अपनी गोल्डन जुबली मनाती है तो सारे कर्मचारी बेहद खुश होते हैं।
examples: Jubilant investors celebrated as the Sensex crossed an all-time high.
Jubilant fans poured onto the streets after the national team won the final.

meaning: Showing good judgment
trick: 'Judge'+'cious' — Judge की तरह सोच-समझकर फैसला लेने वाला।
examples: A judicious use of resources helps a bank survive a crisis.
A judicious teacher knows when to praise a student and when to correct gently.

meaning: A huge, powerful, and overwhelming force
trick: 'Jagannath' — पुरी की जगन्नाथ रथ यात्रा का विशाल रथ, जिसे कोई रोक न सके।
examples: The juggernaut of digital payments has transformed India's banking sector.
The ruling party's election machine rolled on like a juggernaut, crushing every opposition campaign.

meaning: Becoming young or youthful again
trick: 'Juvenile'+'escent' — फिर से Juvenile (जवान) होने वाला।
examples: The new design has a juvenescent appeal that attracts young customers.
The spa promised a juvenescent glow, leaving its elderly guests feeling young again.

hindi: पास-पास रखना (तुलना या अंतर दिखाने के लिए)
meaning: To place side by side for comparison
trick: 'Just'+'Pose' — तुलना करने के लिए दो अलग चीज़ों को बिल्कुल पास-पास रखकर Pose कराना।
examples: The report juxtaposes the bank's current profits with last year's losses.
The museum chose to juxtapose ancient sculptures with modern art to show how styles evolved.

meaning: A commotion or fuss, often over trivial matters
trick: 'Kar'+'Faltu' — छोटी-सी फालतू बात पर हंगामा कर देना।
examples: There was a kerfuffle outside the bank when a customer refused to wear a mask.
