A small kerfuffle broke out at the wedding when two guests claimed the same chair.

meaning: To light a fire or to arouse a feeling
trick: 'Kindle' = 'Candle' — Candle जलाना यानी आग जलाना; मन में उम्मीद की Candle जलाना यानी भावना जगाना।
examples: The teacher's speech kindled a passion for banking in the students.
A single encouraging word from her coach can kindle hope in a nervous young athlete.

meaning: Similar in kind; related
trick: 'Kin' (परिवार) + 'dred' — परिवार जैसा जुड़ाव।
examples: As a kindred spirit, she immediately understood her new colleague's vision.
The two scientists were kindred souls, both driven by a deep love for the stars.

meaning: Relating to or resulting from motion
trick: 'Kinetic Energy' — Physics वाली गतिज ऊर्जा।
examples: The kinetic energy of the market shifted after the RBI announcement.
A rolling ball carries kinetic energy that turns into heat as friction slows it down.

meaning: Destiny or fate
trick: 'Kiss'+'met' — 'Kiss met' वाली किस्मत की मुलाकात।
examples: It was pure kismet that he met his future business partner on a delayed flight.
She believed it was kismet that her lost letter reached the one person who could help.

meaning: Government by thieves
trick: 'Klepto' (Steal) + 'Cracy' (Rule) — चोरों का शासन।
examples: The country suffered under a kleptocracy for decades.
Historians describe the regime as a kleptocracy, since its leaders emptied the national treasury for themselves.

meaning: An uncontrollable urge to steal
trick: 'Klepto' (Steal) + 'Mania' (Madness) — चोरी करने का पागलपन।
examples: The wealthy businessman sought therapy for kleptomania.
The shopkeeper treated the girl gently once he learned her thefts came from kleptomania, not greed.

meaning: A dishonest or unscrupulous man
trick: 'K' silent, 'Nave' = 'Naav' — बीच नदी में नाव रोककर दुगना किराया माँगने वाला बेईमान नाविक।
examples: The finance department was wary of the knave who always found loopholes.
In the old tale, a cunning knave tricked the villagers out of their savings.

hindi: मातमी घंटी की आवाज़ / शोक संकेत
meaning: The sound of a bell, especially for a death or funeral
trick: 'Bell' — Bell (घंटी) की धीमी और मातमी आवाज़।
examples: The news of the founder's death sounded the knell for an era.
The slow knell of the church bell told the village that the old priest had died.

meaning: Praise or credit for an achievement
trick: 'Kudos' = 'Kuddo' — इतनी तारीफ मिली कि खुशी से कूदो!
examples: She received kudos from the CEO for her excellent customer service.
Kudos to the volunteers who cleaned the entire beach before sunrise.

meaning: A complicated network of paths; maze
trick: 'Lab'+'Ring' — Lab के अंदर गोल-गोल Rings जैसे रास्ते, जहाँ से बाहर निकलना मुश्किल।
examples: The bank's loan approval process is a labyrinth of paperwork.
Tourists got lost in the labyrinth of narrow lanes behind the old fort.

meaning: A deep cut or tear in the skin
trick: 'Laser'+'ation' — Laser की तरह फाड़ देने वाला गहरा घाव।
examples: The accident left a deep laceration on the driver's arm.
The nurse cleaned the laceration on the boy's knee before applying a bandage.

meaning: Tearful or inclined to weep
trick: 'Lakh'+'Roz' — जो लाख बार, रोज़ रोता रहे।
examples: The lachrymose farewell speech left many in the audience emotional.
The lachrymose widow wept at every mention of her late husband's name.

meaning: Lacking energy, enthusiasm, or shine
trick: 'Lack'+'Luster' — Luster (चमक) की Lack (कमी) यानी फीका।
examples: The bank's lackluster quarterly results disappointed investors.
The team gave a lackluster performance in the semi-final and lost by ten wickets.

meaning: Using very few words in speech
trick: 'Lack'+'Vani' — जिसकी वाणी में फालतू शब्द न हों बस दो टूक और संक्षिप्त बात कहे।
examples: His laconic "No" ended all hopes of getting a deadline extension.
Asked about his long journey, the laconic farmer only said that it was fine.

meaning: To criticize harshly
trick: 'Lambi'+'Baat' — लंबी-लंबी बातें सुनाकर किसी को बुरी तरह फटकारना।
examples: The RBI lambasted commercial banks for poor customer service.
Critics lambasted the director for turning a brilliant novel into a boring film.

meaning: To express deep regret or grief
trick: 'Lost'+'Moment' — खोए पल को याद करके रोना।
examples: The shareholders lamented the sudden fall in the company's stock price.
Residents lament the loss of the old banyan tree that once shaded the whole street.

meaning: Slow and relaxed, showing little energy
trick: 'Lang'+'Lid' — पलक (Lid) भारी हो जैसे नींद आ रही हो।
examples: The languid pace of the summer afternoon made everyone sleepy.
A languid river wound slowly through the valley as the afternoon heat settled in.

hindi: कमजोर होना / बुरी हालत में पड़े रहना / मुरझाना
meaning: To lose vitality; to be kept in an unpleasant situation
trick: 'Long'+'Wish' — Long (लंबे) समय तक Wish पूरी न हो तो इंसान अंदर से मुरझाने लगता है।
examples: Without fresh funding, the infrastructure project continues to languish.
Many talented students languish in remote villages because they lack access to good teachers.

meaning: Lukewarm or indifferent, especially in religion
trick: 'Lao'+'Dheemi'+'Sun' — न गरम, न ठंडा; उदासीन।
examples: His laodicean attitude toward the temple rituals upset his pious parents.
The laodicean congregation showed up on holidays but cared little for the faith itself.

meaning: Generosity in giving money or gifts
trick: 'Large'+'Yes' — हर माँगने वाले को Large दिल से "Yes" कहना, यानी दानशीलता।
examples: The largesse of the philanthropist helped build three rural schools.
The king's largesse fed hundreds of poor families during the long famine.

meaning: Feeling or showing strong sexual desire
trick: 'Lose'+'Civil' — Civil (सभ्य) व्यवहार Lose कर देना, यानी अश्लील नज़र या टिप्पणी।
examples: The manager was fired for making lascivious comments to female employees.
The film was banned for its lascivious scenes, which the censor board found offensive.

meaning: Existing but not yet visible or active
trick: 'Late'+'nt' — जो Late (बाद में) अचानक बाहर आए।
examples: The audit revealed latent fraud that had been building for years.
The teacher helped uncover the boy's latent talent for music.

meaning: To praise highly
trick: 'Loud'+'Clap' — किसी के शानदार काम पर ज़ोरदार (Loud) ताली बजाकर उसकी प्रशंसा करना।
examples: Global agencies continue to laud India's digital public infrastructure.
Scientists laud the young researcher's discovery as a major step in cancer treatment.

meaning: Deserving praise and commendation

trick: 'नदी' — नदी की तली, यानी किसी चीज़ का सबसे निचला बिंदु। (उल्टा: Zenith = शिखर)
examples: The bank's reputation reached its nadir after the fraud was exposed.
The team reached its nadir after losing ten matches in a row.

hindi: कमजोर / भावुक और कमज़ोर इरादे वाला
meaning: Weakly sentimental or indecisive
trick: 'नरम'+'पोला' — इतना नरम-पोला कि कोई पक्का फ़ैसला ही न ले सके, यानी कमज़ोर और ढुलमुल।
examples: The namby-pamby leadership allowed the fraud to grow unchecked.
The coach scolded the players for their namby-pamby attitude and demanded more determination.

meaning: An entrance porch of an early church
trick: 'Near the Exit' — चर्च में Exit के Near वाला बरामदा।
examples: The narthex of the ancient church was filled with marble carvings.
Pilgrims waited in the narthex until the priest opened the main doors of the church.

meaning: Just beginning to develop; newly formed
trick: 'Naya'+'Saint' — जो इंडस्ट्री या कंपनी अभी नई-नई जन्मी हो और शुरुआती चरण में हो।
examples: Green hydrogen is still a nascent industry in India.
The nascent friendship between the two shy classmates grew stronger over the term.

meaning: Vague and ill-defined
trick: 'Nebula' (धूल का बादल) — कोहरे और बादल जैसा धुंधला और अस्पष्ट।
examples: The startup failed because the founders had only a nebulous idea of the market.
His plans for the future remained nebulous, with no dates or goals written down.

meaning: Wicked and criminal
trick: 'Na'+'Fair' — जो काम Fair (सही) न हो वो दुष्ट और गैर- कानूनी होता है।
examples: Cyber criminals use nefarious methods to steal credit card details.
The detective uncovered a nefarious plot to poison the town's water supply.

meaning: Failing to take proper care
trick: 'Neglect' — जो अपने काम को Neglect करे वो लापरवाह है।
examples: The bank was found negligent in verifying the borrower's documents.
The negligent driver was fined for ignoring the red light near the school.

meaning: So small that it can be ignored
trick: 'Neglect'+'Able' — जिसे Neglect (नज़रअंदाज़) किया जा सके, इतना कम।
examples: The processing fee was negligible compared to the loan amount.
The price difference between the two phones was negligible, so she chose the one she liked.

meaning: A beginner or novice
trick: 'Neo'+'Fight' — जो मैदान में नया-नया Fight करने उतरा हो वो नौसिखिया।
examples: As a neophyte in stock trading, he invested only small amounts.
As a neophyte in the mountaineering club, she was paired with an experienced guide.

meaning: To irritate or annoy
trick: 'Net' — बार-बार Net कटे तो चिढ़ आती है, यानी चिढ़ाना।
examples: The reporter's persistent questions nettled the nervous minister.
His constant humming began to nettle his sister while she studied.

meaning: Very stingy; given in small amounts
trick: 'Nigar'+'Guard' — जो अपनी तिजोरी पर Guard बिठाकर रखे और एक रुपया भी खर्च न करे।
examples: The workers went on strike after receiving a niggardly bonus on Diwali.
The niggardly host served watery tea and a single biscuit to each guest.

meaning: Existing in name only; very small
trick: 'No' + 'Money' — जब पैसा No (नहीं) हो, तो सिर्फ नाम का (Nominal) शुल्क लिया जाए।
examples: The bank charged a nominal fee for opening the account.
Visitors can enter the museum for a nominal charge of just five rupees.

meaning: To surprise and confuse someone completely
trick: 'No'+'Plus Point' — ऐसा सवाल कि कोई Plus Point न सूझे और दिमाग सुन्न हो जाए, यानी हक्का-बक्का।
examples: The sudden resignation of the CEO nonplussed the entire board.
The child's sharp question nonplussed the speaker, who stood silent for several seconds.

meaning: A sentimental longing for the past
trick: 'नौ साल'+'जिया' — गाँव में बचपन के नौ साल जिया, उन्हें याद करके मन भर आना।
examples: The retired banker was filled with nostalgia when he saw his old branch.
The smell of mango pickle filled her with nostalgia for her grandmother's kitchen.

meaning: A person new to an activity
trick: 'नव' (नया)+'Ice' — पहली बार Ice पर फिसलता नया खिलाड़ी, यानी नौसिखिया।
examples: As a novice trader, he started with very small investments.
The novice swimmer clung to the pool's edge while the coach encouraged him.

meaning: Harmful or poisonous
trick: 'Knock' — फैक्ट्री से निकलने वाली हानिकारक गैस जो सेहत को Knock-out कर दे।
examples: The factory was shut down for releasing noxious fumes into the air.
Noxious gas leaked from the old storage tank, forcing nearby families to evacuate.

meaning: Of no value or importance
trick: 'No'+'Get' — जिससे कुछ भी Get (हासिल) न हो, यानी बेकार और मूल्यहीन।
examples: Without proper enforcement, the new law is nugatory.
Their apology was nugatory, since the damage had already been done and nothing could repair it.

meaning: To make legally void
trick: 'Null' (शून्य) + 'ify' — किसी चीज़ को शून्य बना देना यानी रद्द करना।
examples: The court nullified the fraudulent loan agreement signed under pressure.
A single mistake in the paperwork could nullify the whole contract.

meaning: Stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion
trick: 'Ob'+'Durable' — Durable पत्थर जैसा जो कभी न पिघले, यानी ज़िद्दी और हठी।
examples: The defaulter remained obdurate and refused to sell his property to pay the loan.
The obdurate old farmer refused to sell his land, no matter how high the offer rose.

meaning: Respectful obedience or deference
trick: 'Obey'+'Sense' — बड़ों को Obey करने की Sense, यानी झुककर प्रणाम और आदर करना।
examples: The courtiers made obeisance before the king upon his entry.
Villagers bowed in obeisance as the revered saint walked through the market.

meaning: To make something unclear or confusing
trick: 'Ob'+'Fuss'+'Gate' — सीधी बात को बड़े-बड़े शब्दों में घुमाया कि सब उलझ गए।
examples: Corrupt companies often use complex accounting tricks to obfuscate their real losses.
The politician tried to obfuscate the issue with long, confusing sentences.

meaning: A notice of someone's death, often with a brief biography
trick: 'अब'+'इति' — जीवन की 'इति' (अंत) के बाद अख़बार में छपी श्रद्धांांजलि वाली ख़बर।
examples: The newspaper published a moving obituary of the bank's founder.
She cut her teacher's obituary out of the morning paper and kept it in her diary.

meaning: Not influenced by personal feelings; fair
trick: 'Object'+'ive' — Object (लक्ष्य) पर नज़र, भावना से दूर।
examples: The audit report gave an objective view of the bank's performance.
A good judge must stay objective and decide only on the evidence presented.

meaning: Indirect; slanting
trick: 'O'+'लीक' — 'लीक से हटकर', यानी सीधा नहीं बल्कि तिरछा या घुमा-फिराकर।
examples: The manager made oblique references to the upcoming layoffs.
She gave an oblique hint about the surprise party without saying a direct word.

hindi: मिटा देना / पूरी तरह खत्म करना
meaning: To destroy completely
trick: 'Ob'+'Literal' — किसी चीज़ को Literally खत्म कर देना यानी मिटा देना।
examples: The fraud completely obliterated the family's life savings.
The fierce storm threatened to obliterate the small coastal village from the map.

meaning: The state of being forgotten
trick: 'ओ! भूल' — "ओ, भूल गए!" यानी पूरी तरह भुला दिया जाना (विस्मृति)।
examples: Great achievements of the old era have faded into oblivion.
The old singer sank into oblivion, and few people remember his songs today.

meaning: Darkness or obscurity
trick: 'O! Scary Room' — घुप्प अंधेरा कमरा = गहरा अंधकार।
examples: The obscurum of the cave made exploration dangerous.
He felt his way through the obscurum of the cellar, unable to see even his own hands.

meaning: To beg or entreat earnestly
trick: 'Ob'+'Sake' — "For God's Sake!" कहकर बार-बार गिड़गिड़ाना, यानी विनती करना।
examples: The farmers obsecrated the bank manager for more time to repay the loan.
The prisoner began to obsecrate the guards, begging them to deliver a letter to his mother.

meaning: Excessively eager to please; servile
trick: 'Ob'+'See'+'Yes' — बॉस की हर बात पर "Yes बॉस Yes बॉस" करने वाला चापलूस।
examples: He surrounded himself with obsequious assistants who never questioned him.
The obsequious waiter bowed so often that the diners felt embarrassed.

meaning: A funeral ceremony
trick: 'Last'+'Sequence' — जीवन का आख़िरी Sequence, यानी अंतिम संस्कार। (Obsequious = चापलूस)
examples: The obsequies of the founder were attended by top bankers from across India.
Thousands gathered at the river bank for the obsequies of the beloved poet.

meaning: No longer in use; outdated
trick: 'Ab'+'Sholay' — शोले फिल्म के ज़माने की मशीनें अब पुरानी (अप्रचलित) हो चुकी हैं।
examples: Passbooks are slowly becoming obsolete due to mobile banking apps.
Typewriters have become obsolete in most offices, replaced by laptops and printers.

meaning: Noisy and difficult to control
trick: 'Obstruction'+'Noise' — जो रास्ते में Obstruction करके भारी Noise (शोर) मचाए।
examples: Security was called to remove the obstreperous customer from the branch.
The obstreperous children ran through the library shouting, ignoring every request for silence.

meaning: To prevent or avoid
trick: 'Avoid it' — मुसीबत को पहले ही Avoid कर देना, ताकि वो आए ही नहीं।
examples: Proper documentation can obviate the need for lengthy verification.
Building a bridge would obviate the need for a long detour around the lake.

meaning: Asserting authority in an annoying, meddlesome way
trick: 'Office' — ऑफिस में जो बिना मांगे हर किसी के काम में टांग अड़ाए।
examples: Nobody likes an officious colleague who gives unwanted advice.
The officious guard stopped every visitor to ask questions that were none of his business.

meaning: To stare at someone in a lecherous or offensive way
trick: 'O'+'गोल' — आँखें 'O' जैसी गोल-गोल करके किसी को घूरना।
examples: It is considered rude to ogle at people in public places.
The shopkeeper told the boys not to ogle the girls walking past his stall.

meaning: Involving a great deal of effort and difficulty
trick: 'Owner' — घर के मालिक के कंधों पर पूरे परिवार के खर्च का भारी बोझ होता है।
examples: Small businesses complained about the onerous compliance rules.
Carrying heavy water pots up the hill every day was an onerous task for the women.

meaning: Not able to be seen through; not transparent
trick: 'O'+'Pack' — जिसके अंदर कुछ भी दिखे नहीं, बस एक Pack (पैक) जैसा हो।
examples: The bank's pricing structure was so opaque that customers felt cheated.
The opaque curtains blocked the sunlight, leaving the room completely dark.

meaning: Well-timed; favorable
trick: 'Opportunity'+'Tune' — बिल्कुल सही अवसर और उपयुक्त समय पर उठाया गया कदम।
examples: The dip in stock prices provided an opportune moment for long-term investors to buy.
The rain arrived at an opportune moment, just as the farmers finished sowing seeds.

meaning: Expressing scorn or criticism
trick: 'Oppose'+'Bribe' — Bribe लेने वाले का Oppose करते हुए कड़ी निंदा।
examples: The opprobrious comments against the board hurt investor confidence.
The newspaper printed opprobrious remarks about the player after his dropped catch.

meaning: Harsh criticism and public disgrace
trick: 'Oppose'+'Bribe'+'um' — घोटाला पकड़े जाने पर उस प्रोफेशनल को पूरे समाज में भारी निंदा झेलनी पड़ी।
examples: The bank faced public opprobrium for charging hidden fees from poor farmers.
The mayor faced widespread opprobrium after he was caught hiding relief supplies.

meaning: Luxurious and wealthy
trick: 'Oh!'+'Pool' — घर में Swimming Pool देखकर सब बोलें "Oh!", यानी अमीरी और ठाठ-बाट।
examples: The company hosted an opulent dinner for its foreign investors.
The maharaja's opulent palace had golden doors and chandeliers in every hall.

hindi: डोलना / झूलना / दो विचारों के बीच भटकना
meaning: To swing back and forth; waver between opinions
trick: 'इस'+'उस'+'Late' — कभी इस तरफ़, कभी उस तरफ़ झूलते रहे और फ़ैसला Late हो गया।
examples: The rupee continued to oscillate between 83 and 84 against the dollar.
The pendulum began to oscillate slowly, swinging from one side of the clock to the other.

meaning: To kiss
trick: 'Oscar' + 'Late' — ऑस्कर जीतने के बाद एक्ट्रेस ने खुशी से एक-दूसरे को किस किया।
examples: The couple osculated in the park, unaware of the people around.
In the old play, the prince bent down to osculate the hand of the queen.

meaning: Showy; designed to impress
trick: 'Us'+'Tent' — शादी में इतना महंगा Tent सिर्फ दिखावे के लिए लगाया गया।
examples: Despite being a billionaire, he avoids an ostentatious lifestyle.
Her ostentatious wedding, with a hundred cars and fireworks, was the talk of the town.

meaning: Done or shown openly; not hidden
trick: 'Over'+'Vert' — जो बात छुपी न हो बल्कि Over (ऊपर) से सबको साफ दिख रही हो।
examples: There was no overt sign of financial trouble before the company collapsed.
The teacher's overt favouritism towards a few students upset the rest of the class.

meaning: Relating to a classical architectural style
trick: 'Palace' — Palace जैसी खंभों वाली शानदार इमारत।
examples: The bank's Palladian facade attracted heritage lovers from across the city.
The Palladian villa, with its symmetrical columns and classical porch, looked like a Roman temple.

hindi: कम करना / दर्द या लक्षण घटाना
meaning: To reduce the severity of pain or a problem without curing
trick: 'पल' — दवा जो पल भर दर्द कम करे, जड़ से इलाज नहीं।
examples: The scheme palliates poverty but does not solve its root cause.
Painkillers can palliate the ache of arthritis, though they cannot cure the disease.

meaning: Small or meager to the point of being insignificant
trick: 'पल्ले'+'Try' — कितनी भी Try करो, पल्ले कुछ न पड़े, यानी बहुत मामूली रकम।
examples: A paltry fine of ₹500 is no deterrent for large corporate frauds.
Farmers were angry at the paltry price offered for their wheat crop.

meaning: A remedy for all problems or diseases
trick: 'Pan'+'Cure' — Pan (सब) बीमारियों का Cure (इलाज) करने वाली रामबाण दवा।
examples: Digital payments are not a panacea for all financial inclusion challenges.
Many people treat turmeric milk as a panacea, though it cannot cure every illness.

meaning: A speech or text of elaborate praise
trick: 'Pan'+'e'+'Geet' — सबके (Pan) सामने तारीफ़ के गीत गाना, यानी भव्य प्रशंसा।
examples: The retiring chairman received a heartfelt panegyric from his successor.
The poet composed a panegyric praising the generosity of the village headman.

meaning: A typical example, pattern, or model
trick: 'Para'+'Design' — सोचने या काम करने का Design (ढांचा)। Paradigm Shift = सोच में बड़ा बदलाव।
examples: Mobile banking has brought a paradigm shift in how people manage money.
The village cooperative became a paradigm for other communities hoping to share water fairly.

meaning: A perfect model of excellence
trick: 'Para'+'Gone' — मजबूती के मामले में पैरागॉन चप्पल सालों से एक आदर्श उदाहरण रही है।
examples: The former governor was considered a paragon of integrity and wisdom.
Everyone saw the nurse as a paragon of patience and kindness.

meaning: More important than anything else
trick: 'Para'+'Mount' — जो Para (सबसे ऊपर) Mount (पहाड़) की तरह सर्वोच्च हो।
examples: Customer trust is paramount for any banking institution.
During a flood, saving human lives is paramount, and property comes second.

meaning: A social outcast
trick: 'Paraya' — जिसे समाज या ग्रुप ने 'पराया' मानकर बाहर निकाल दिया हो यानी बहिष्कृत।
examples: After the massive accounting fraud, the founder became a corporate pariah.
After betraying his friends, he became a pariah in the small town.

meaning: Extremely unwilling to spend money
trick: 'Purse'+'Money' — जो Purse से Money निकालने में जान दे दे वो महा कंजूस है।
examples: The parsimonious businessman refused to upgrade the old office computers.
The parsimonious uncle reused tea bags and switched off every light the moment we left a room.

meaning: Prejudiced in favor of a particular cause
trick: 'Party'+'San' — जो हर बात में अपनी Party (पार्टी) का ही पक्ष ले।
examples: A central bank must remain non-partisan and free from political pressure.
The partisan referee gave every doubtful decision in favour of the home team.

meaning: Scarcity; a small quantity
trick: 'Pav'+'City' — पूरी सिटी में सिर्फ पाव भर अनाज बचा है यानी भारी कमी।
examples: Due to a paucity of time, the committee could not discuss all the proposals.
A paucity of rainfall this year has left the wells almost dry.

meaning: Strange or odd; belonging exclusively to someone
trick: 'Pick'+'Uliar' — हर जगह से Pick करके अलग और अजीब।
examples: The customer had a peculiar habit of counting coins three times.
A peculiar noise from the attic kept the family awake all night.

meaning: Expressing disapproval or insult
trick: 'Page'+'Zero'+'Rate' — किसी के काम को ज़ीरो रेटिंग देकर उसके लिए अपमानजनक शब्द बोलना।
examples: Avoid using pejorative terms when writing a professional review.
Calling someone lazy is a pejorative remark that can wound a student's confidence.

meaning: Transparently clear
trick: 'Pearl'+'Lucid' — Pearl (मोती) की तरह Lucid (बिल्कुल साफ) और स्पष्ट।
examples: The RBI governor gave a pellucid explanation of the new policy.
The pellucid lake showed fish swimming ten feet below the surface.

meaning: A strong liking or preference
trick: 'Pen'+'Chant' — Pen से Chant (गीत) लिखने का बड़ा लगाव।
examples: She has a penchant for solving complex mathematical puzzles.
My brother has a penchant for collecting old coins from every country he visits.

meaning: Feeling sincere regret for wrongdoing
trick: 'Pain'+'it' — गलती का Pain दिल में हो, यानी सच्चे मन से पछताने वाला।
examples: The penitent defaulter wrote an apology letter to the bank manager.
The penitent boy admitted breaking the window and offered to pay for it.

meaning: Extremely poor or stingy
trick: 'Penny'+'urious' — Penny-Penny जोड़कर जीने वाला।
examples: The penurious landlord refused to fix the leaking roof for years.
The penurious miser lived in a dark hut to avoid paying for electricity.

meaning: Extreme poverty
trick: 'Pen'+'Nahi' — जिसके पास एक Pen खरीदने तक का पैसा न हो वो घोर गरीबी में है।
examples: Bad investments drove the once-wealthy family into penury.
The poet died in penury, though his verses later became famous across the country.

hindi: निर्णायक / बिना बहस के हुक्म देने वाला
meaning: Insisting on immediate attention or obedience
trick: 'Pre'+'Emperor' — Emperor (सम्राट) की तरह तुरंत हुक्म देना, कोई बहस नहीं।
examples: The peremptory tone of the email offended even senior employees.
The captain gave a peremptory order to leave the ship at once.

meaning: Lasting or existing for a long time; recurring
trick: 'Per'+'Annual' — जो Per (हर) Annual (साल) खिलता रहे यानी बार-बार होने वाला।
examples: Inflation is a perennial problem that central banks constantly battle.
Water shortage is a perennial worry for residents of the dry coastal town.

meaning: Done routinely with little interest
trick: 'Par'+'Function' — किसी Function में बिना मन के बस हाज़िरी लगाना।
examples: The guard did a perfunctory check of the bags at the gate.
He gave a perfunctory nod to the guests and went back to his phone.

meaning: Full of danger or risk
trick: 'Per'+'Loose' — पहाड़ पर चलते हुए पैर (Per) Loose हुआ तो बहुत खतरा! यानी खतरनाक।
examples: Investing in unregulated markets without research is a perilous gamble.
The climbers began the perilous descent along a narrow, icy ledge.

meaning: The outer limits or edge of something
trick: 'Peri'+'Ferry' — Peri (चारों तरफ) Ferry (नाव) घूमती है यानी बाहरी घेरा।
examples: Small towns on the periphery of metro cities are seeing rapid bank branch expansion.
Wild deer sometimes wander into the periphery of the city near the forest.

hindi: पारगम्य / जिससे होकर पानी या हवा पार जा सके
meaning: Allowing liquids or gases to pass through
trick: 'Paar'+'Me'+'Able' — जिसके पार में पानी जाने में Able हो, जैसे छन्नी यानी पारगम्य।
examples: The roof proved to be permeable during heavy monsoon rains.
Sandy soil is permeable, so rainwater drains quickly into the ground.

meaning: To spread throughout
trick: 'Permit' — परमिट मिलते ही कंपनी का माल पूरे बाज़ार में फैल गया।
examples: Optimism began to permeate the financial markets after the tax cuts.
The aroma of fresh bread began to permeate the whole street.

meaning: Having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual way
trick: 'Par'+'Nishan' — चोट का ऐसा निशान जो शरीर के अंदर ही अंदर घातक असर छोड़े।
examples: Corruption has a pernicious effect on the economic growth of a nation.
Gossip can have a pernicious effect on friendships, slowly poisoning trust.

hindi: बनाए रखना / स्थायी बनाना / जारी रखना
meaning: To make something continue indefinitely
trick: 'Per'+'Petu'+'Ate' — पेटू हमेशा Ate (खाता) रहता है, कभी रुकता नहीं यानी जारी रखना।
examples: Such outdated policies only perpetuate inequality in the banking system.
Stories that mock certain communities only perpetuate harmful stereotypes among children.

meaning: Having keen insight and good judgment
trick: 'Par'+'Spy' — Spy की तरह तेज़ नज़र और तेज़ बुद्धि रखने वाला।
examples: A perspicacious investor spotted the market trend before anyone else.
The perspicacious detective noticed the muddy footprint that everyone else had overlooked.

hindi: प्रासंगिक / उचित / मुद्दे से जुड़ा हुआ
meaning: Directly relevant to a matter at hand
trick: 'Per'+'Tika' — जो बात मुद्दे पर टिकी (Tika) रहे, इधर- उधर न भटके यानी प्रासंगिक।
examples: The manager asked only pertinent questions during the interview.
She answered every pertinent question the committee asked and ignored the irrelevant ones.

meaning: To disturb or trouble greatly
trick: 'Per'+'Turbine' — Turbine अचानक रुक जाए तो पूरा सिस्टम परेशान और बेचैन हो जाता है।
examples: The sudden rate hike perturbed small borrowers across the country.
The strange footsteps outside the window began to perturb the lonely old woman.

meaning: To spread through all parts of something
trick: 'Par'+'Vaidya' — वैद्य जी की जड़ी-बूटियों की खुशबू पूरे घर में फैल गई।
examples: A sense of fear pervaded the stock exchange during the crisis.
A feeling of excitement seemed to pervade the stadium before the opening ceremony.

hindi: बारिश के बाद मिट्टी की सोंधी खुशबू
meaning: The pleasant smell of earth after rain
trick: 'Pet'+'Ichor' — Pet (पालतू) कुत्ता भी बारिश के बाद मिट्टी की खुशबू सूंघने दौड़ पड़ता है।
examples: The petrichor after the first monsoon shower refreshed the whole town.
Children ran outside to enjoy the petrichor rising from the dusty courtyard after the first rain.

meaning: Childishly sulky or bad-tempered
trick: 'Petty'+'Ulant' — छोटी-छोटी (Petty) बातों पर बच्चों की तरह चिढ़ने वाला।
examples: The customer service agent calmly handled the petulant complaints of the buyer.
The petulant boy threw his toys on the floor because dinner was late.

meaning: A fact or situation that is observed to exist or happen
trick: 'Phenomenal' — जो कुछ इतना अद्भुत और असाधारण हो कि वो Phenomenal (गज़ब) लगे।
examples: The sudden surge in digital payments is a global phenomenon.
A solar eclipse is a rare natural phenomenon that draws crowds to observatories.

meaning: Calm and unemotional, especially in difficult situations
trick: 'Phlegm' (कफ) — जिसे कफ की तरह ठंडा और शांत रहना आता है।
examples: Even during the bank robbery, the cashier remained remarkably phlegmatic.
The phlegmatic pilot calmly announced the turbulence and kept flying as usual.

meaning: The highest point of success
trick: 'Pin'+'Nacle' — जो Pin (सुई) की नोक की तरह सबसे ऊपर और शिखर पर हो।
examples: Winning the banking award was the pinnacle of his long career.
Winning the Olympic gold was the pinnacle of the wrestler's career.

meaning: Calm and not easily upset
trick: 'Place'+'Aid' — शांत Place पर Aid मिले तो मन शांत रहता है।
examples: The placid lake reflected the mountains perfectly.
The placid cow chewed grass while the noisy festival passed by.

meaning: Expressing sadness or sorrow
trick: 'Plain'+'Tive' — Plain (सीधी) और दुख भरी आवाज़ में Complain करना।
examples: The plaintive cries of the farmers moved the entire audience.
A plaintive song from the street singer made passers-by pause with sadness.

meaning: Seeming reasonable or probable
trick: 'Plaus'+'Able' — बहाना ऐसा हो जो सुनने में बिल्कुल भरोसेमंद और सच लगे।
examples: He gave a plausible explanation for missing the project deadline.
Her story about the missed bus sounded plausible, so the teacher let her go.

meaning: Easily bent or influenced
trick: 'Ply'+'able' — Ply (मोड़ना) आसान हो जिसे।
examples: Young minds are pliable and can be shaped with the right education.
Wet clay is pliable and can be moulded into any shape by a potter.

meaning: A dangerous or difficult situation
trick: 'P'+'Light' — जिसकी Life में P (पैसा) और Light (रोशनी) दोनों खत्म हो जाएं वो दुर्दशा में है।
examples: The farmers were in a terrible plight after the crop failure.
The government sent tents and blankets to ease the plight of the flood victims.

meaning: To fall very quickly and steeply
trick: 'Plum'+'Met' — Plum धड़ाम से गिरा, ज़मीन से Met।
examples: The company's shares plummeted by 20% today.
Temperatures plummet at night in the desert, falling far below freezing.

meaning: Deeply affecting; emotionally moving
trick: 'Poison'+'Ant' — Poison (ज़हर) की तरह दिल को चुभने वाला दुख।
examples: The documentary showed a poignant reunion of refugees with their families.
It was a poignant moment when the old soldier saluted the flag one last time.

meaning: A person of great and varied learning
trick: 'Poly' (Many) + 'History' — जिसे हर विषय का इतिहास और ज्ञान हो।
examples: The polyhistor was consulted by the government on multiple complex issues.
Leonardo is often called a polyhistor, since he mastered painting, anatomy and engineering.

meaning: Self-important and arrogant
trick: 'Pump'+'ous' — Pump (पंप) की तरह हवा भरा घमंडी।
examples: His pompous speeches about his achievements bored everyone.
The pompous host kept reminding guests of his famous relatives and his grand house.

meaning: To think about something deeply
trick: 'Pond'+'er' — Pond (तालाब) के किनारे बैठकर गहराई से सोचना।
examples: The RBI is pondering over the impact of rate cuts on inflation.
She sat by the river to ponder whether to accept the job abroad.

meaning: Dealing with things sensibly and realistically
trick: 'Practical'+'Magic' — सिर्फ Magic नहीं, Practical तरीके से हल निकालना।
examples: A pragmatic banker focuses on repayment capacity, not just collateral.
A pragmatic farmer chooses crops that suit the soil instead of chasing fashionable ones.

meaning: An introductory statement or preliminary part
trick: 'Pre' (पहले) — संविधान की Preamble सबसे पहले आती है यानी प्रस्तावना (GA में भी काम आएगा)।
examples: The preamble of the banking regulation act explains its objectives.
Before the main agenda, the chairman read a short preamble thanking everyone for coming.

meaning: Not securely held; dangerously unstable
trick: 'Pre'+'Care' — जिस रास्ते पर Pre (पहले से) Care (सावधानी) रखनी पड़े।
examples: Heavy borrowing put the company in a precarious financial position.
The hiker's precarious position on the slippery rock made his friends hold their breath.

meaning: An earlier event serving as an example for future cases
trick: 'President' — President का फैसला हमेशा भविष्य के मुकदमों के लिए पूर्व उदाहरण बनता है।
examples: The court ruling set a legal precedent for similar banking fraud cases.
Allowing one latecomer without a penalty might set a precedent that others will demand.

hindi: जल्दबाज़ी में करना / अचानक तेज़ी से घटाना
meaning: To cause to happen suddenly or prematurely
trick: 'Pre'+'Sip'+'Tate' — चाय Sip करते ही बिना सोचे-समझे जल्दी से कोई काम हड़बड़ी में कर देना।
examples: The sudden rumor could precipitate a panic withdrawal of deposits.
A careless remark during the meeting could precipitate a quarrel between the two partners.

meaning: To prevent from happening
trick: 'Pre'+'Include' — Include (शामिल) होने से Pre (पहले) ही रोक देना।
examples: Strict audit rules preclude any possibility of hidden corruption.
A broken leg will preclude him from joining the school's annual race.

hindi: समय से पहले विकसित (बौद्धिक रूप से)
meaning: Mature or developed earlier than usual
trick: 'Pre'+'Conscious' — जो बच्चा उम्र से पहले ही बड़ों जैसी समझदारी दिखाए।
examples: The precocious ten-year-old boy already understands how the stock market works.
The precocious girl was reading newspapers at five and solving puzzles meant for adults.

meaning: A difficult or unpleasant situation
trick: 'Pre'+'Dikkat'+'Ment' — चारों तरफ दिक्कत ही दिक्कत यानी कठिन स्थिति।
examples: Losing his wallet put him in a difficult financial predicament.
Stranded without a ticket at midnight, the traveller was in an awkward predicament.

meaning: A preference or special liking for something
trick: 'Pre'+'Dil'+'Election' — आपका दिल पहले से ही जिस चीज़ को चुन ले यानी विशेष झुकाव।
examples: Conservative investors have a strong predilection for gold and fixed deposits.
The chef has a predilection for spicy dishes and adds chillies to nearly everything.

meaning: Outstanding; above all others
trick: 'Pre'+'Main' — जो सबसे Pre (आगे) और सबसे Main हो यानी सर्वश्रेष्ठ।
examples: SBI holds a preeminent position in the Indian banking industry.
She became the preeminent sprinter of her generation, winning every national title.

meaning: A right or privilege exclusive to a particular individual or class
trick: 'Pre' (पहले से) + 'Right' — जो अधिकार जन्म या पद से पहले से ही मिला हो।
examples: It is the manager's prerogative to approve or reject the leave request.
Choosing the team captain is the prerogative of the coach, not the players.

meaning: Having foreknowledge of events
trick: 'Pre'+'Science' — जिसे Pre (पहले) ही Science की तरह भविष्य का पता चल जाए।
examples: A prescient analyst predicted the banking crisis months before it occurred.
His prescient warning about the flood saved many families who moved to higher ground.

meaning: To speak evasively or avoid telling the truth
trick: 'Pre'+'Variable' — जो बात हर बार Variable (बदलती) रहे वो टालना और सच छुपाना है।
examples: The witness tried to prevaricate when asked about the money trail.
Instead of admitting the mistake, the clerk began to prevaricate and change the subject.

meaning: Complete honesty and integrity
trick: 'Prove'+'Biti' — जिसने हर कसौटी पर अपनी ईमानदारी Prove कर दी हो।
examples: Financial probity is the most important quality for a bank officer.
The judge was admired across the country for his probity and refusal to accept gifts.

meaning: A natural tendency to do something
trick: 'Pro'+'Click' — Reels पर बार-बार Click करने की आदत यानी झुकाव / प्रवृत्ति।
examples: Successful traders have a natural proclivity for risk management.
The child has a proclivity for taking apart clocks to see how they work.

meaning: To delay or postpone action
trick: 'Pro'+'Crash' — हर काम कल पर टाला तो Exam से पहले तैयारी Crash हो गई यानी टालना।
examples: Students who procrastinate often fail to clear banking exams on time.
If you procrastinate, the homework piles up and the night before the deadline becomes a nightmare.

meaning: Wastefully extravagant with money
trick: 'Product'+'Gal' — फालतू Products खरीद कर पैसा पानी की तरह बहाने वाला फिज़ूलखर्च।
examples: His prodigal spending habits quickly emptied his bank account.
The prodigal son returned home after squandering his inheritance on parties and gifts.

meaning: Recklessly extravagant with money
trick: 'Profit'+'Gate' — Profit की Gate खोलकर पैसे पानी की तरह फिज़ूलखर्ची में उड़ा दिए।
examples: His profligate lifestyle soon drained his family's generational wealth.
The profligate heir wasted his fortune on racehorses and lavish parties within a few years.

meaning: Very deep or intense; showing great insight
trick: 'Pro'+'Found' — Professor ने रिसर्च करके बहुत गहरा और गंभीर ज्ञान खोज निकाला।
examples: The digital revolution had a profound impact on traditional banking.
The old monk's words left a profound impression on the young visitors.

hindi: तेज़ी से फैलना / बहुसंख्या में बढ़ना
meaning: To increase rapidly in number
trick: 'Pro'+'Life'+'Rate' — जीवन की दर इतनी तेज़ी से बढ़ना कि हर तरफ फैल जाए।
examples: UPI-enabled online apps continue to proliferate across small towns.
Mosquitoes proliferate quickly in stagnant water left standing after the heavy monsoon rains.

meaning: Producing a great deal of something
trick: 'Pro'+'Leaf' — जिस पेड़ पर ढेरों Leaf (पत्ते) और फल आएँ यानी बहुत उत्पादक।
examples: He is a prolific writer who has published twenty books on finance.
The prolific painter completed nearly three paintings every week for forty years.

meaning: A natural inclination or tendency
trick: 'Pro'+'Pension' — बैंक की नौकरी चाहने वालों का स्वाभाविक झुकाव Pension की तरफ होता है।
examples: Indian households have a high propensity to save money in gold.
Cats have a natural propensity to chase anything that moves quickly across the floor.

meaning: A person who advocates for something
trick: 'Pro'+'Component' — जो किसी Component (विचार) के Pro (समर्थन में) हो।
examples: He is a strong proponent of digital currency in India.
As a proponent of free education, she campaigned for more government schools.

meaning: Conformity to proper behavior and morals
trick: 'Proper'+'Priority' — जो हर काम में Proper तरीका और Priority अपनाए वो उचित आचरण करता है।
examples: Officials must maintain complete propriety in all financial dealings.
The guests behaved with propriety, standing quietly as the national anthem played.

meaning: To officially forbid something
trick: Doctor 'Prescribe' करता है = ये लो; सरकार 'Proscribe' करती है = ये मत लो (Ban)।
examples: The government proscribed the use of certain chemicals in food processing.
Many schools proscribe mobile phones during class hours to keep students focused.

meaning: Readily taking on different forms or roles
trick: 'Pro'+'Teen' — Teenager रोज़ नया रूप बदलता है।
examples: The protean nature of digital banking demands adaptable skills.
The protean actor played a king, a beggar and a robot with equal ease.

meaning: Great skill or expertise in a particular activity
trick: 'Pro'+'Wise' — जो Pro की तरह Wise होकर काम करे उसमें कुशलता है।
examples: The new CEO was hired for his prowess in digital banking.
The young archer's prowess amazed spectators, as she hit the target ten times in a row.

meaning: Nearness in space or time
trick: 'Proxy' — Proxy लगाने वाला दोस्त हमेशा पास बैठता है।
examples: The proximity of the new bank branch to the market boosted daily transactions.
The house's proximity to the railway station made it popular among daily commuters.

meaning: Wise and careful in making decisions
trick: 'Prudent' ≈ 'Student' — समझदार Student हर कदम सोच-समझकर उठाता है।
examples: It is prudent to invest a portion of your income in fixed deposits.
It is prudent to carry an umbrella during the monsoon season.

meaning: The study of elections and voting
trick: 'See'+'Poll'+'Logy' (P silent) — Poll (चुनाव) को See करके Study करना यानी चुनाव-विज्ञान।
examples: Psephology helps banks predict economic policies based on election results.
Her interest in psephology led her to analyse voting patterns across the district.

meaning: Childishly silly and immature
trick: 'Pure'+'Child' — बच्चों की Pure (मासूम) और कभी- कभी मूर्खतापूर्ण बातें।
examples: His puerile arguments failed to convince the bank board.
The comedian's puerile jokes about burps made the adults groan.

meaning: Eager to fight or argue
trick: 'Pug'+'Nacious' — Pug (कुत्ता) की तरह लड़ने को तैयार।
examples: His pugnacious attitude often landed him in trouble with management.
The pugnacious little dog barked at every stranger and challenged larger dogs in the lane.

meaning: Having great power or influence
trick: 'Power'+'Sant' — Power से भरा संत यानी शक्तिशाली।
examples: The puissant central bank can move markets with a single statement.
The puissant emperor commanded armies that stretched across three continents.

hindi: नियम-निष्ठ / बारीकी से नियम मानने वाला
meaning: Showing great attention to detail and correct behavior
trick: 'Punctual'+'ious' — Punctual की तरह हर नियम का पालन।
examples: The punctilious auditor flagged every minor discrepancy in the report.
The punctilious host arranged every fork and napkin exactly in its proper place.

meaning: Having a sharply strong taste, smell, or comment
trick: 'Punch'+'Gent' — जिसका Punch (वार) बहुत तीखा हो वो कटु है।
examples: The editorial was full of pungent criticism of the new tax policy.
The pungent smell of garlic frying drifted from the kitchen.

meaning: Cowardly; lacking courage
trick: 'Push'+'Lena'+'Mat' — "मुझे आगे Push मत करना, मुझे डर लगता है" यानी कायर।
examples: The pusillanimous manager refused to take a stand against corruption.
The pusillanimous soldier fled at the first sound of gunfire.

meaning: A difficult, complex, or dangerous situation
trick: 'Quack'+'Mire' — बतख कीचड़ के दलदल में फँस गई यानी ऐसी कठिन स्थिति जिससे निकलना मुश्किल।
examples: Taking multiple credit cards can trap you in a financial quagmire.
After the heavy rain, the village road turned into a quagmire that trapped bullock carts.

meaning: Attractively unusual or old-fashioned
trick: 'Q'+'Ancient' — पुराना (Ancient) पर प्यारा, अनोखा।
examples: The quaint village bank still used handwritten ledgers.
We stayed in a quaint cottage with a thatched roof and a tiny wooden gate.

meaning: A state of uncertainty or confusion
trick: 'Kaun'+'Dairy' — कौन सी Dairy खरीदूँ इसी दुविधा में पड़ गया।
examples: The board was in a quandary over whether to merge with the rival bank.
Faced with two equally good job offers, Meera found herself in a real quandary for days.

hindi: संगरोध / अलगाव (बीमारी से बचने के लिए)
meaning: A state of isolation to prevent the spread of disease
trick: 'Quarter' + 'Ensure' — एक Quarter (कमरे) में Ensure (पक्का) करके किसी को अलग रखना।
examples: The travelers were put in quarantine for two weeks after arriving.
Cattle from the infected farm were kept in quarantine until the veterinarian declared them healthy.

hindi: रद्द करना / निरस्त करना / कुचल देना
meaning: To reject or void, especially a legal decision
trick: 'Squash' — किसी चीज़ को पैर के नीचे दबाकर कुचल देना या कोर्ट द्वारा आदेश रद्द कर देना।
examples: The High Court decided to quash the fraudulent charges against the employee.
The magistrate refused to quash the order, so the shop remained sealed pending the appeal.

meaning: To put an end to something, usually by force
trick: 'Cool' — पुलिस ने दंगे को दबाकर Cool कर दिया।
examples: The bank issued a statement to quell rumours of insolvency.
Police used tear gas to quell the riot before it spread to neighbouring streets.

meaning: Complaining in a whining manner
trick: 'Query' — जो आदमी हर बात पर सौ Query निकाले और रोना रोए।
examples: The customer care executive patiently handled the querulous caller.
The querulous old tenant complained about the noise, the stairs, the weather and even the milk.

meaning: Inactive or dormant; temporarily at rest
trick: 'Quiet'+'Saint' — शांत Saint की तरह जो बिल्कुल स्थिर और निश्चल बैठा हो।
examples: The real estate market remained quiescent during the monsoon season.
The volcano has been quiescent for centuries, so villagers built homes on its fertile slopes.

meaning: The most perfect example of a quality
trick: 'Quint'+'Essential' — Most Essential यानी सबसे Perfect उदाहरण, जैसे Maggi = Quintessential hostel food।
examples: The Taj Mahal is the quintessential symbol of Indian architecture.
Masala chai at a roadside stall is the quintessential evening ritual of many Indian towns.

meaning: A traitor who collaborates with the enemy
trick: 'Quisling' ≈ 'किसलिए?' — "किसलिए अपना देश बेचा?" गद्दार से यही पूछा जाता है।
examples: The quisling leaked the bank's strategic plans to a competitor.
History remembers him as a quisling who opened the city gates to the invading army.

meaning: To tremble or shake with a slight rapid motion
trick: 'Quick' + 'Waver' — डर या ठंड से Quick Waver (तेज़ी से कांपना)।
examples: Her voice quivered with emotion as she gave the farewell speech.
The leaves began to quiver as the first gusts of the storm swept through the orchard.

meaning: Impractical and idealistic in an unrealistic way
trick: 'Quick'+'Exotic' — एक Quick दिन में सारे Exotic (विदेशी) देश घूमने का प्लान यानी ख्याली।
examples: Doubling your money in two days is a quixotic dream.
His quixotic plan to cycle around the world with no money worried his parents.

meaning: Showing mild confusion or amusement
trick: 'Quiz' — Quiz के सवाल जैसा हैरान करने वाला भाव।
examples: She gave a quizzical look when told about the strange new policy.
The teacher raised a quizzical eyebrow when the boy claimed a dog had eaten his homework.

meaning: Occurring every day; ordinary
trick: 'Quote'+'Daily' — Daily Quote होने वाली रोज़मर्रा की बात।
examples: The quotidian tasks of a bank clerk can become monotonous.
For farmers, the quotidian routine begins before sunrise with milking the cows and feeding the cattle.

meaning: Uncontrollably exuberant; boisterous
trick: 'Ram'+'Bunk' — Ram ने Class Bunk की और पूरे Hostel में उधम मचाया यानी शरारती।
examples: The rambunctious interns made the workplace lively every morning.
A rambunctious group of puppies tumbled over the cushions and knocked the vase off the table.

meaning: Long-lasting bitterness or hatred
trick: 'Rank' — जब दोस्त की Rank आपसे अच्छी आ जाए तो मन में द्वेष पैदा होता है।
examples: Despite losing the election, he spoke without any rancor toward his opponent.
Years after the property dispute, the two brothers still spoke with rancor about their father's will.

meaning: Characterized by bitterness and hatred
trick: 'Rank'+'Rous' — Rank (ऊंचा) बढ़ने पर Rancour (द्वेष) भी बढ़ता है।
examples: Their rancorous divorce battle dragged on for years.
The rancorous debate in parliament ended with members shouting insults across the aisle.

meaning: A close and harmonious relationship
trick: 'Rapport' ≈ 'Report' — Boss से अच्छा तालमेल हो तो Report भी अच्छी आती है।
examples: The manager built a strong rapport with the branch's rural customers.
A good teacher quickly establishes rapport with shy students so they feel safe asking questions.

meaning: A mischievous or dishonest person
trick: 'Rascal' — Rascal (शरारती) से भी बढ़कर धूर्त बदमाश।
examples: The rapscallion was caught trying to hack the bank's ATM.
Grandmother called the grinning boy a little rapscallion after he hid all her knitting needles.

meaning: To formally approve or confirm
trick: 'Rate'+'Verify' — जब Rate तय हो जाए तो उसे सबकी मंज़ूरी से Verify और पक्का करना।
examples: The RBI needs parliament to ratify the new banking amendment.
Member countries must ratify the climate treaty before it can take legal effect.

meaning: To reason logically and methodically
trick: 'Ratio' — Quant के Ratio सवाल तर्क से हल करना।
examples: Great leaders ratiocinate before taking any major policy decision.
The detective sat silently by the fire to ratiocinate over every clue before naming the culprit.

meaning: The fundamental reason or justification
trick: 'Ration'+'Analyze' — Ration (हिस्सा) बांटने से पहले सरकार का मुख्य तर्क और आधार क्या है?
examples: The finance minister explained the rationale behind the new tax slabs.
Please explain the rationale for moving the match to the evening instead of the morning.

meaning: Making a harsh, loud noise
trick: 'Rock'+'ous' — Rock concert का कर्कश शोर।
examples: The raucous laughter from the next room kept him awake all night.
A raucous crowd of fans cheered loudly as the home team scored in the final minute.

meaning: Extremely hungry
trick: 'Raven'+'ous' — Raven (कौवा) की तरह हमेशा भूखा।
examples: After the long trek, the group was ravenous and devoured the meal.
The ravenous lion tore into the carcass after three days without a successful hunt.

hindi: अस्वीकार करना / झिड़की / साफ मना करना
meaning: An abrupt refusal of an offer or advance
trick: 'Re'+'Buff' — Buff (मज़बूत) दीवार की तरह Re (फिर से) किसी को पीछे धकेल कर मना करना।
examples: The startup's application for a banking license was rebuffed by the regulator.
He tried to befriend the new neighbour but met with a cold rebuff each time.

meaning: To refute or argue against
trick: 'Re'+'But' — 'But' बोलकर विरोध करना।
examples: The bank issued a statement to rebut the allegations of mis-selling.
The lawyer stood up to rebut the witness's claim with a signed receipt and dated photographs.

meaning: Stubbornly defiant of authority
trick: 'Re'+'Calcium' — Calcium वाली सख्त हड्डी की तरह अकड़ा, किसी के आगे न झुके यानी हठीला।
examples: The central bank imposed heavy penalties on recalcitrant banks.
The recalcitrant mule refused to climb the trail no matter how hard the guide pulled.

meaning: A period of economic decline
trick: 'Recess' — स्कूल में खेलकूद की छुट्टी (Recess) की तरह मार्केट में आर्थिक मंदी छा जाना।
examples: Many tech companies laid off workers to prepare for a potential recession.
During the recession, many families postponed buying cars and cut down on restaurant meals.

meaning: The tendency to relapse into criminal behavior
trick: 'Re'+'CD' — पुरानी CD की तरह अपराधी बार-बार वही अपराध Re-play करे।
examples: Strict laws aim to reduce recidivism among financial fraudsters.
The prison's skill-training programme helped lower recidivism, as fewer released inmates returned to crime.

meaning: Given or felt by each toward the other; mutual
trick: 'Re' + 'Sip' + 'Proposal' — जब दोनों तरफ से Sip (चाय) पीकर Proposal (समझौता) किया जाए।
examples: The two banks signed a reciprocal agreement to share ATM networks.
Friendship is reciprocal: you cannot expect loyalty from others if you never offer any.

meaning: Preferring to live alone and avoid company
trick: 'Exclusive' — जो खुद को सबसे अलग (Exclusive) करके अकेले कमरे में बंद रखे।
examples: The billionaire founder is known for his reclusive lifestyle.
The reclusive poet lived alone in a mountain cabin and rarely answered letters.

meaning: Difficult to understand; obscure
trick: 'Record'+'Code' — जो बात Code language में Record हो, आम आदमी न समझ पाए यानी गूढ़।
examples: The legal document was full of recondite terms that needed a lawyer to explain.
The professor's lecture on quantum field theory was too recondite for first-year students.

meaning: A source of help in a difficult situation
trick: 'Re'+'Course' — फिर से Course (रास्ता) खोजना।
examples: The bank had no recourse but to write off the bad loan.
With the landlord refusing to repair the roof, the tenants had no recourse except the consumer court.

meaning: Cowardly or disloyal
trick: 'Re'+'Create' — जो फिर से Create (बहादुरी) न कर सके, यानी कायर।
examples: The recreant soldier was stripped of his medals for abandoning his troop.
The recreant knight deserted his king on the eve of battle and fled the kingdom.

hindi: बीमारी या समस्या का फिर उभरना
meaning: The return of something unpleasant after a period of absence
trick: 'Re'+'Crude' — Crude Oil के दाम फिर से (Re) बढ़ गए यानी पुरानी समस्या का फिर उभरना।
examples: The recrudescence of inflation worries the RBI.
Doctors warned of a recrudescence of dengue as the rains returned to the city.

meaning: To correct something wrong
trick: 'Right'+'ify' — जो सही (Right) न हो उसे ठीक करना।
examples: The bank promised to rectify the billing error within 24 hours.
The editor promised to rectify the mistake in tomorrow's newspaper with a clear correction.

meaning: Refusing to submit to authority
trick: 'Refuse'+'Ant' — लाइन में चलने से Refuse करने वाली Ant (चींटी) यानी नियम न मानने वाला।
examples: The recusant clerk refused to follow the new banking protocol.
The recusant priest refused to swear loyalty to the new church and was jailed.

meaning: Unnecessary because it's already done or replaced
trick: 'Re'+'Done'+'Dent' — जो काम पहले ही Done हो चुका है उसे दोबारा करना फालतू और अनावश्यक है।
examples: Manual ledger entries have become redundant with core banking systems.
After the machines were installed, many manual packing jobs in the factory became redundant.

meaning: Shining brightly
trick: 'Re'+'Full'+'Gent' — Full चमकता दूल्हा (Gent)।
examples: The refulgent gold coins sparkled under the vault's lights.
The refulgent sun rose over the sea, turning the waves into sheets of molten gold.

meaning: To prove something wrong or false
trick: 'Refuse' — सबूत दे कर किसी के झूठे आरोप को Refuse करना यानी खंडन करना।
examples: The bank issued a press release to refute the rumors of a data leak.
Scientists gathered fresh data to refute the claim that the river was safe for drinking.

hindi: नीचे धकेलना / कम महत्व का पद
meaning: To assign to a lower position or rank
trick: 'Rail'+'Gate' — उसे बड़े ऑफिस से हटाकर रेलवे गेट पर ड्यूटी दे दी (दर्जा घटाना)।
examples: After the poor performance, he was relegated to a junior role.
The club was relegated to the second division after losing seven matches in a row.

meaning: Continuing in a determined way without stopping
trick: 'Relentless' ≈ 'Rest-less' — बिना Rest किए लगातार मेहनत करना यानी अथक।
examples: The team's relentless effort resulted in clearing the banking exam on the first try.
The relentless rain flooded the lower streets and showed no sign of easing for days.

meaning: Closely connected to the matter at hand
trick: 'Related' — जो बात मुद्दे से Related हो।
examples: Only relevant documents should be attached to the loan application.
Keep your answer relevant to the question and avoid wandering into unrelated stories.

meaning: To voluntarily give up something
trick: 'Re'+'Link'+'Quit' — Link तोड़कर Quit कर देना।
examples: The director was forced to relinquish his post after the scandal.
The old king refused to relinquish the throne even when his health failed.

meaning: The process of correcting or improving something
trick: 'Remedy'+'ation' — Remedy (इलाज) की प्रक्रिया।
examples: The bank began remediation of its faulty loan records after the audit.
Soil remediation at the old factory site took five years before children could play there.

meaning: Negligent in the performance of duty
trick: 'Re'+'Miss' — काम को Miss करके लापरवाह होना।
examples: The auditor was found remiss in checking the high-value transactions.
It would be remiss of me not to thank the volunteers who worked all night.

meaning: To protest or complain against something
trick: 'Re'+'Monster' — Monster जैसी गुस्से से आपत्ति जताना।
examples: The employees remonstrated against the sudden change in working hours.
Parents gathered outside the school to remonstrate with the principal about the sudden fee hike.

meaning: Feeling sincere regret for wrongdoing
trick: 'Re'+'Pen' — Pen से गलती की, अब पछता रहा है।
examples: The repentant defaulter wrote an apology letter to the bank manager.
The repentant boy returned the stolen pen and promised never to take anything again.

meaning: An unintended consequence of an event or action
trick: 'Re'+'Cushion' — गेंद Cushion पर मारो तो Re (वापस) उछलकर आती है यानी किए का नतीजा।
examples: Defaulting on a loan has serious financial repercussions.
Cutting down the forest had grave repercussions, including soil erosion and the loss of wildlife.

meaning: Full or well-supplied with something
trick: 'Re'+'Complete' — पूरी तरह Complete भरा हुआ।
examples: The bank's vault was replete with gold reserves during the festive season.
The old library was replete with rare manuscripts, maps and handwritten diaries.

meaning: A temporary relief from pain or trouble
trick: 'Re'+'Pray' — फिर से प्रार्थना करने पर मन को राहत मिलती है।
examples: The tax cut offered a brief reprieve to small businesses.
The sudden cloud cover gave the sweating marathon runners a welcome reprieve from the heat.

meaning: To express disappointment or blame
trick: 'Re'+'Approach' — गलत तरीके से काम Approach करोगे तो बॉस से फटकार मिलेगी।
examples: His conduct at the bank has always been beyond reproach.
She looked at him with quiet reproach when he arrived two hours late to her recital.

meaning: To reject or refuse to accept
trick: 'Re'+'पूड़ी' — फिर से पूड़ी दी तो साफ मना कर दिया।
examples: The company repudiated all responsibility for the data breach.
The minister was quick to repudiate the rumour that he planned to resign.

meaning: To officially cancel or revoke
trick: 'Re'+'Send' — ऑर्डर खराब निकला तो वापस Send कर दिया और डील रद्द कर दी।
examples: The government decided to rescind the controversial tax law.
The university decided to rescind its offer after discovering the applicant had forged his certificates.

meaning: Able to recover quickly from difficulties
trick: 'Re'+'Silent' — Fail होकर रोना नहीं, चुपचाप (Silent) फिर से (Re) तैयारी में लग जाना यानी मज़बूत।
examples: The Indian banking sector proved resilient during the global crisis.
Mangrove forests are resilient and regrow quickly even after fierce cyclones batter the coast.

meaning: Firm and determined in purpose
trick: 'Resolution' — नए साल का Resolution लेने के बाद वो इरादे पर दृढ़ है।
examples: The RBI remained resolute in its fight against inflation.
Resolute despite the pain, the climber pushed on toward the summit through the blizzard.

meaning: Deep and full in sound
trick: 'Re'+'Sound' — मंदिर की घंटी का Sound बार-बार (Re) गूंजता है यानी गूंजने वाला।
examples: The chairman's resonant voice commanded attention in every meeting.
The temple bell gave a deep, resonant note that echoed across the valley.

meaning: A short period of rest or relief
trick: 'Rest'+'pite' — Rest (आराम) की छोटी सी घड़ी।
examples: The interest rate cut provided some respite to small borrowers.
Nurses at the busy hospital rarely got a respite from the stream of patients.

meaning: A renewed rise or revival
trick: 'Re'+'Surge' — किसी चीज़ का फिर से Surge (उछाल) मारकर उठ खड़ा होना।
examples: There is a strong resurgence in digital lending startups this year.
The city saw a resurgence of interest in handloom clothing after the fashion week.

meaning: To fight back or take revenge
trick: 'Re'+'Tally' — हिसाब Tally (बराबर) करना: उसने मारा, मैंने वापस मारा यानी बदला लेना।
examples: The country threatened to retaliate against the new trade tariffs.
The villagers chose not to retaliate when the rival team jeered at them, and simply played on.

meaning: Not revealing thoughts or feelings readily
trick: 'Rati'+'Sent' — जो भावनाएं रत्ती भर भी बाहर न भेजे यानी कम बोलने वाला।
examples: The finance minister was reticent about the upcoming budget plans.
Usually reticent in class, Arun surprised everyone by speaking passionately about his village.

meaning: To reduce costs or staff
trick: 'Re'+'Trim' — कंपनी ने खर्च और स्टाफ को Trim (काट- छाँट) कर दिया यानी छंटनी।
examples: The bank decided to retrench 200 employees to cut operating costs.
Facing falling sales, the textile mill was forced to retrench nearly a third of its workers.

meaning: To give something a new and improved form
trick: 'Re'+'Camp' — पुराने कैंप को सुधार कर नया रूप दिया।
examples: The bank plans to revamp its mobile application completely.
The municipality will revamp the old railway station with new waiting halls and better lighting.

meaning: Feeling deep respect and awe
trick: 'River' — गंगा नदी के प्रति लोग सम्मानपूर्ण भाव रखते हैं।
examples: The employees listened in reverent silence as the founder spoke.
Pilgrims climbed the steps in reverent silence, bowing before the ancient shrine.

meaning: Referring to something in an offensive, vulgar manner
trick: 'Rib'+'Bald' — Rib (पसली) और Bald (गंजा) पर भद्दा मज़ाक।
examples: The comedian's ribald jokes offended several guests at the formal event.
The sailors sang ribald songs in the tavern, making the shy waiter blush.

meaning: Widespread or common, especially of something bad
trick: 'Rife' ≈ 'Wi-Fi' — Wi-Fi की तरह हर कोने में फैला हुआ (अक्सर बुरी चीज़ें: Corruption is rife)।
examples: The industry is rife with rumors of upcoming mergers.
The old port town was rife with stories of ghosts and hidden treasure.

meaning: Strong, healthy, and vigorous
trick: 'Robot' — रोबोट शरीर से मज़बूत होते हैं।
examples: The economy is showing robust recovery after the pandemic.
Her robust health, built on years of walking and simple food, amazed the doctors.

meaning: Involving or limited to basic principles
trick: 'Rude' + 'Mentary' — जो बिल्कुल शुरुआती और Rude (कच्चा) हो।
examples: He has only a rudimentary understanding of the stock market.
The villagers crossed the stream on a rudimentary bridge made of two logs and a rope.

meaning: Expressing regret or sorrow
trick: 'रो'+'Full' — आँखें रोने से Full, यानी पछतावे से भरा।
examples: He gave a rueful smile when reminded of his missed opportunity.
The goalkeeper wore a rueful grin as he watched the easy shot slip through his fingers.

meaning: To think deeply about something
trick: 'Rumi'+'Nate' — Rumi की शायरी की तरह गहराई से सोचना।
examples: The CEO ruminated on the merger proposal for weeks before deciding.
On the long train journey, she had time to ruminate on her choices and her future.

meaning: A clever trick or stratagem
trick: 'Ruse' ≈ 'रोज़' — चालाक लोमड़ी रोज़ नई चाल चलकर धोखा देती है यानी चाल / युक्ति।
examples: The fraudster used a clever ruse to obtain the customer's OTP.
The thief used the ruse of a broken-down car to distract the guard.

meaning: Excessively sweet or sentimental
trick: 'Sugar'+'ine' — Sugar जैसी चीनी में डूबी झूठी मिठास।
examples: Her saccharine comments felt fake to the experienced team.
The film's saccharine ending, with everyone hugging and crying, felt too sweet to believe.

meaning: Violation of something sacred
trick: 'Sacred'+'lie' — Sacred (पवित्र) चीज़ पर Lie (झूठ) यानी अपवित्रता।
examples: Stealing from a temple donation box is considered a sacrilege.
Many villagers regarded the felling of the sacred banyan tree as an unforgivable sacrilege.

meaning: Wise and insightful, especially in practical matters
trick: 'Sage' — साधु-संत बहुत बुद्धिमान और दूरदर्शी होते हैं।
examples: A sagacious leader always prepares the company for future crises.
The sagacious village elder settled the land dispute with a solution that pleased both families.

meaning: Most noticeable or important
trick: 'Sail'+'ent' — Sail (नाव) की तरह सबसे ऊपर उभरी हुई बात।
examples: The report highlighted the salient features of the new banking policy.
Before the exam, she underlined the salient points of each chapter in red ink.

meaning: Health-giving; promoting well-being
trick: 'Sallu' — सल्लू भाई की तरह फिट रहने के लिए स्वास्थ्यप्रद हवा चाहिए।
examples: He moved to the hills to enjoy the salubrious climate.
Doctors advised the patient to spend a month by the sea for its salubrious air.

meaning: Making a show of being morally superior
trick: 'Saint'+'Money' — Saint जैसे दिखकर Money के पीछे भागने वाला पाखंडी।
examples: His sanctimonious speeches about integrity ring hollow given his scandals.
Nobody enjoyed dinner with the sanctimonious guest who lectured everyone on their eating habits.

meaning: Optimistic and positive
trick: 'Sang'+'Win' — सब लोग Sang (साथ) हैं तो ज़रूर Win करेंगे ऐसी आशावादी सोच।
examples: Economists are sanguine about India's GDP growth this year.
Despite two failed attempts, the coach remained sanguine about his team's chances in the finals.

meaning: Mocking and cynical in a bitter way
trick: 'Sir'+'Tonic' — बॉस ने काम बिगड़ने पर कड़वे ताने (व्यंग्य) का टॉनिक पिलाया।
examples: He gave a sardonic smile when told that the project was delayed again.
His sardonic reply, that he adored waiting in queues, made the clerk look away.

meaning: Related to tailoring or style of dress
trick: 'Sir'+'torial' — Sir की तरह Tailored (सिले हुए) बेहतरीन कपड़े।
examples: His sartorial elegance made him stand out at the corporate event.
The prince was admired for his sartorial taste, always appearing in perfectly tailored suits.

hindi: तृप्त करना / पूरी तरह संतुष्ट करना
meaning: To satisfy fully or to excess
trick: 'Saat'+'Ate' — सात रोटियां खा लीं अब पेट पूरी तरह तृप्त हो गया।
examples: The company increased production to satiate the growing market demand.
No amount of praise could satiate the actor's hunger for attention.

meaning: Gloomy or morose in temperament
trick: 'Saturday'+'ine' — Saturday की थकान जैसी उदास और चिड़चिड़ी शक्ल।
examples: His saturnine expression made everyone nervous before the audit.
The saturnine old gatekeeper greeted visitors with a scowl and never wished anyone good morning.

meaning: The study of excrement or obscene literature
trick: 'Scatter'+'Logy' — इधर-उधर Scattered (बिखरी) गंदगी का अध्ययन।
examples: The researcher's interest in scatology was considered very weird by his friends.
The professor warned that the book's heavy use of scatology made it unsuitable for school libraries.

meaning: A person with superficial knowledge
trick: 'Science'+'List' — जिसे Science के बस नामों की List याद हो, समझ ज़ीरो यानी सतही ज्ञानी।
examples: His sciolism was exposed during the detailed policy discussion.
A true scholar admits what he does not know, unlike the sciolist who pretends to know everything.

meaning: To examine very closely
trick: 'Screw'+'Tiny' — Screw जैसी छोटी चीज़ भी Tiny से Tiny जांचना।
examples: Auditors scrutinize every transaction above ten lakh rupees.
The customs officer began to scrutinize the traveller's passport page by page.

meaning: Making or spreading scandalous claims to damage a reputation
trick: 'Scary'+'Lies' — डरावने (Scary) झूठ (Lies) फैलाकर किसी को बदनाम करना।
examples: The politician sued the magazine for publishing scurrilous rumors about him.
The scurrilous pamphlet accused the schoolteacher of crimes he had never committed.

meaning: Involving much sitting and little physical activity
trick: 'Sit'+'entry' — दिन भर Sit (बैठे) रहने वाला।
examples: A sedentary lifestyle is a major cause of lifestyle diseases.
Doctors urge office workers with sedentary jobs to stand up and stretch every hour.

meaning: Inciting rebellion against authority
trick: 'Desh'+'Dishoom' — जो अपने देश की सरकार से ढिशूम-ढिशूम (बगावत) करे वो राजद्रोही है।
examples: He was arrested for spreading seditious messages on social media.
The colonial government banned the seditious newspaper and arrested its editor.

hindi: परिश्रमी / लगन से काम करने वाला
meaning: Showing dedication and diligence
trick: 'Sedu' (सदा) + 'Lous' — सदा लगन से पढ़ने वाला Aspirant यानी परिश्रमी।
examples: Her sedulous efforts finally paid off when she cleared the RBI Grade B exam.
The sedulous gardener weeded, watered and pruned every morning until the whole terrace bloomed.

meaning: To isolate or take away for safekeeping
trick: 'Seize'+'Quarter' — सामान Seize (ज़ब्त) करके अलग Quarter में रख दिया।
examples: The court ordered the assets to be sequestered during the trial.
The jury was sequestered in a hotel so that no one could influence their verdict.

meaning: The occurrence of happy events by chance
trick: 'Serene'+'Dip'+'ity' — Serene मन से Dip करते हुए अचानक कुछ खोज लेना।
examples: Meeting her future business partner on a delayed flight was pure serendipity.
It was pure serendipity that she found her grandmother's lost letters while searching for a book.

meaning: Calm, peaceful, and untroubled
trick: 'Sea'+'Rene' — Sea (समुद्र) की तरह शांत और निर्मल।
examples: Her serene expression calmed the nervous team before the audit.
The lake was serene at dawn, with not a ripple disturbing its glassy surface.

meaning: Using very long words; long-winded
trick: 'Pedal' — यह शब्द खुद इतना लंबा है कि बोलने में Cycle के Pedal जितनी मेहनत लगे यानी लंबे शब्दों वाला।
examples: The sesquipedalian circular confused even senior officers.
The speaker's sesquipedalian style, full of needlessly long words, left the villagers bewildered.

meaning: Having sharp judgment; clever and practical
trick: 'Shr' (शेर) — शेर जैसा तेज़ और चालाक दिमाग।
examples: A shrewd investor knows when to buy and when to sell.
The shrewd shopkeeper guessed from the customer's hurry that he would pay a higher price.

meaning: To smile in a silly or coy way
trick: 'Simple'+'Smile' — झूठी Simple Smile बनाकर बात करना।
examples: The salesman simpered while trying to push a useless product.
The boy began to simper at the teacher, hoping to be excused from homework.

meaning: Having many curves and turns
trick: 'S'+'inuous' — 'S' अक्षर की तरह मुड़ा हुआ, जैसे सांप या पहाड़ी सड़क यानी टेढ़ा-मेढ़ा।
examples: A sinuous mountain road led to the remote hill town.
A sinuous river wound through the green valley before spilling into the sea.

meaning: To shed or cast off
trick: 'Slow'+'F' — पुरानी Skin को Slow Slow करके झड़ना।
examples: The company sloughed off its unprofitable divisions during the restructuring.
Snakes slough their skin several times a year as they grow.

meaning: A sudden, sharp decline in value or performance
trick: 'Slip'+'Jump' — स्लिप होकर जंप किया तो गिरावट हुई।
examples: The housing market is experiencing a severe slump.
The team's batting slump continued as they lost five consecutive matches.

meaning: Showing attentive care or concern
trick: 'Saloni'+'Tension' — माँ बच्चों की भलाई को लेकर हमेशा चिंतित रहती है।
examples: The bank manager was very solicitous about the senior citizen's comfort.
The solicitous nurse kept checking whether the elderly patient needed another blanket.

meaning: Having enough money to pay all debts
trick: 'Solve'+'Rent' — जो Rent और Loan Solve कर सके वो financially सक्षम है।
examples: The company remained solvent even during the economic downturn.
Careful budgeting helped the small family firm stay solvent through two bad harvests.

meaning: Sleepy or causing sleep
trick: 'Sleep'+'olent' — Sleep आने वाला, नींद से भरा।
examples: The soporific lecture left the audience somnolent by the end.
The somnolent cat lay stretched on the warm windowsill, barely opening an eye at the noise.

meaning: Tending to induce sleep
trick: 'So'+'Fikar' — बिना Fikar के So जाओ क्योंकि ये लेक्चर नींद लाने वाला है।
examples: The long presentation after lunch had a soporific effect on the audience.
The soporific hum of the train soon put the weary passengers to sleep.

meaning: Dirty, filthy, or morally degraded
trick: 'Sada' — सड़ा हुआ और गंदा काम (अनैतिक या घिनौना)।
examples: The investigation revealed the sordid details of the money laundering scam.
The newspaper exposed the sordid truth behind the charity, which pocketed most of the donations.

hindi: दिखावे में सही (पर वास्तव में गलत) / भ्रामक
meaning: Apparently plausible but actually misleading
trick: 'Special'+'Show' — Special Show करके जो ऊपर से सही दिखे पर अंदर से गलत हो।
examples: The fraudster used specious arguments to trap innocent investors.
His specious excuse that the dog ate the tickets fooled nobody.

meaning: Occurring at irregular intervals
trick: 'Spot'+'Radical' — कभी-कभार Spot पर कुछ Radical (अचानक) हो जाए यानी छिटपुट।
examples: Sporadic internet issues disrupted the online banking services today.
Sporadic showers fell through the afternoon, but the cricket match was never stopped.

meaning: False or fake; not genuine
trick: 'Spoon'+'Real' — Spoon में Real चांदी नहीं है बल्कि Spurious (नकली) है।
examples: Customers must beware of spurious calls asking for OTPs.
The museum discovered that the so-called ancient coin was a spurious copy made last year.

meaning: Not moving, flowing, or developing
trick: 'Stag' (Stuck) — गड्ढे में Stuck (अटका) हुआ पानी।
examples: Wage growth has been stagnant over the last five years.
Mosquitoes bred in the stagnant water that had collected in the old tyres.

meaning: Lack of activity, growth, or development
trick: 'Stuck'+'Nation' — जब पूरे Nation की Economy Stuck हो जाए यानी ठहराव / मंदी।
examples: Economic stagnation worries policymakers more than moderate inflation.
After years of stagnation in the village, the new road finally brought trade and visitors.

meaning: Serious, quiet, and rather old-fashioned
trick: 'Stay' — जो एक जगह स्थिर Stay करे उछल-कूद न करे वो गंभीर और शांत होता है।
examples: Banking is traditionally seen as a staid and serious profession.
The staid old professor wore the same grey coat and walked the same path each day.

meaning: A loyal, reliable, and hardworking supporter
trick: 'Stall'+'War' — जो हर War (मुसीबत) में आपकी Stall (दुकान/पार्टी) के आगे चट्टान की तरह खड़ा रहे।
examples: Ratan Tata was a stalwart of the Indian corporate world.
She was a stalwart of the local football club, attending every practice for thirty years.

meaning: A publicly stated attitude or position on an issue
trick: 'Stand' — इस मुद्दे पर आपका स्टैंड (रुख) क्या है?
examples: The Monetary Policy Committee kept a neutral stance on rates.
The union softened its stance after the company offered a better pay package.

meaning: Outstanding; exceptionally good
trick: 'Star' — Star जैसा चमकदार और शानदार।
examples: The bank posted stellar profits this quarter despite global headwinds.
The young pianist gave a stellar performance that earned a standing ovation from the audience.

meaning: Something that encourages activity or growth
trick: 'Steam' — गाड़ी में स्टीम देकर उसे आगे बढ़ाने के लिए प्रोत्साहन और बूस्टर देना।
examples: The government announced a financial stimulus package for small industries.
A small cash prize acted as a stimulus, and the students worked harder than ever.

meaning: Randomly determined; involving chance
trick: 'Stock'+'Astic' — Stock Market के भाव Random ऊपर-नीचे होते हैं यानी यादृच्छिक।
examples: The stock market is highly stochastic and hard to predict.
Weather patterns are partly stochastic, so even the best forecasters sometimes get tomorrow wrong.

meaning: Showing little emotion or reaction
trick: 'Stone'+'Solid' — पत्थर जैसा Solid दिल जिस पर सुख- दुख का असर न दिखे।
examples: The accused remained stolid as the judge read out the verdict.
The stolid farmer showed no joy or worry while the officials announced the compensation.

meaning: A clever plan to achieve something
trick: 'Strategy'+'Gem' — Strategy का Gem (रत्न) यानी चालाकी से बनाई योजना।
examples: The company used a clever stratagem to win the market share.
The general's stratagem of lighting hundreds of fires made the enemy think a huge army waited.

hindi: तेज़ और कर्कश आवाज़ वाला / तीखा
meaning: Loud, harsh, and grating
trick: 'Strike'+'Student' — जब Students हड़ताल पर बैठते हैं तो तेज़ और कर्कश नारे लगाते हैं।
examples: The opposition raised strident objections to the privatization bill.
The strident ring of the alarm clock jolted the sleeping boy awake.

meaning: Strict and precise; rules that must be followed
trick: 'Strict'+'Gent' — जो Gentleman बहुत strict हो, वो सख्त नियमों में रहता है।
examples: The RBI has introduced stringent rules for loan approvals.
Airports follow stringent security checks, and no passenger is allowed to skip them.

meaning: To support financially, usually to reduce cost
trick: 'Sub'+'Sidha' — Sub (कम) कीमत पर Sidha (सीधा) लाभ देने के लिए subsidize करते हैं।
examples: The government decided to subsidize electric vehicles to boost adoption.
The state will subsidize school meals so that poor children do not go hungry.

meaning: Deception used to achieve a goal
trick: 'Sab'+'Tar'+'Fuse' — कमरे के सब Tar Fuse कर दिए ताकि अंधेरे में चाल चलकर भाग सके।
examples: The journalist used subterfuge to gain entry into the secret meeting.
The spies entered the palace through subterfuge, dressed as musicians in the royal band.

meaning: So delicate or precise as to be difficult to analyze
trick: 'Sub' (नीचे) + 'Tle' — जो चीज़ नीचे छिपी हो और आसानी से समझ न आए।
examples: The difference between the two banking policies is very subtle.
A subtle smell of jasmine drifted through the room, so faint that few noticed it.

meaning: An excessive amount of something
trick: 'Sur'+'Feet' — इतना खाना कि सिर से Feet (पैर) तक भर जाए यानी ज़रूरत से ज़्यादा।
examples: A surfeit of cheap loans led to a bubble in real estate.
A surfeit of sweets at the festival left the children feeling sick.

meaning: A sudden, powerful forward or upward movement
trick: 'Surgeon' — Surgeon की fees हर साल Surge (तेज़ बढ़ोतरी) होती है।
examples: There was a sudden surge in digital payments this month.
A sudden surge of floodwater swept the fragile bridge away within minutes.

meaning: Done secretly to avoid attention
trick: 'Surprise'+'Suspicious' — चोरी-छिपे कुछ Suspicious करना।
examples: The employee made surreptitious attempts to steal confidential data.
She cast a surreptitious glance at her neighbour's answer sheet when the invigilator turned away.

meaning: Continuing for an extended period
trick: 'Sus'+'Ten' — जो लगातार बिना रुके Ten (दस) सालों तक टिके रहकर चले।
examples: India needs sustained double-digit growth to become a developed nation.
Sustained effort over many months, not last-minute cramming, produced her excellent exam results.

meaning: A whispering or rustling sound
trick: 'सुसुर-सुसुर' — कान में धीमी फुसफुसाहट की आवाज़।
examples: The susurrus of the river calmed the anxious traders.
The susurrus of leaves in the evening breeze lulled the children to sleep.

meaning: A person who flatters to gain advantage
trick: 'Sick'+'Funt' — Sick कर देने वाली Fun की झूठी तारीफ करने वाला।
examples: The sycophant at the office always agreed with the boss, even when wrong.
The prince was surrounded by sycophants who praised every foolish decision he made.

meaning: Understood without being stated
trick: 'Take'+'it' — 'बस Take it' कहे बिना ही बात मान लेना।
examples: There was a tacit agreement between the two partners on the merger.
The neighbours had a tacit understanding that nobody would play loud music after ten.

meaning: Habitually silent or uncommunicative
trick: 'Taxi'+'Turn' — टैक्सी ड्राइवर चुपचाप Taxi Turn करता रहा पूरे रास्ते एक शब्द नहीं बोला।
examples: My new manager is a taciturn man who speaks only when necessary.
The taciturn fisherman answered every question with a nod and rarely wasted a word.

meaning: An object thought to bring good luck
trick: 'Talis'+'Man' — वो चीज़ जो Man को Lucky बनाए, जैसे Exam वाला Lucky Pen यानी ताबीज़।
