examples: The old merchant believed his ring was a talisman of good fortune.
The cricketer kissed the small talisman his mother gave him before walking out to bat.

meaning: Equivalent in seriousness to; virtually the same as
trick: 'Tanta'+'Amount' — उतना ही Amount यानी बराबर: Paper Leak करना = Cheating के बराबर।
examples: Refusing to sign the audit report is tantamount to admitting guilt.
Ignoring the doctor's warning is tantamount to inviting a heart attack.

meaning: To gradually reduce something in amount
trick: 'Tape' — Tape का रोल इस्तेमाल करते-करते धीरे-धीरे पतला होता जाता है यानी कम होना।
examples: The central bank decided to taper its bond purchases.
The road begins to taper near the summit until only one vehicle can pass.

meaning: Delayed; slow to act
trick: 'Turtle'+'Lady' — कछुए जैसी Lady, सदा लेट।
examples: A tardy reply to the customer's complaint worsened the issue.
The tardy student slipped into the classroom twenty minutes after the lecture had begun.

meaning: Losing shine or reputation
trick: 'Tar'+'Nish' — चांदी पर Tar लगा तो धूमिल हो गई।
examples: The bank's tarnished reputation made customers wary of it.
The tarnished silver spoons gleamed again after an hour of polishing with lemon and salt.

meaning: Recklessly bold or daring
trick: 'Tame'+'various' — Tame (शांत) न रहकर Various जोखिम लेने वाला।
examples: Investing all savings in one stock was a temerarious decision.
The temerarious sailor set out in a tiny boat to cross the stormy channel.

meaning: Excessive confidence or boldness
trick: 'Time'+'Rity' — Time के सामने भी न डरने वाली ढिठाई।
examples: He had the temerity to question the chairman's decision in public.
The new recruit had the temerity to correct the veteran captain in front of the whole team.

meaning: Defensible and reasonable
trick: 'Tenant' — जिस पर Tenant टिक सके, यानी जो टिक सके।
examples: The theory is tenable only if the data is interpreted correctly.
The theory that the sun circles the earth was no longer tenable after Galileo's observations.

meaning: Holding firmly; persistent and determined
trick: 'Teen'+'Rassi' — तीन रस्सियों से बंधी गांठ की तरह जो लक्ष्य को मज़बूती से पकड़े।
examples: Only tenacious aspirants succeed in clearing competitive exams.
The tenacious terrier refused to let go of the rope, however hard the children pulled.

meaning: The quality of holding firmly; persistence
trick: 'Ten'+'acity' — Ten (दस) गुना मज़बूती से पकड़े रहने का भाव।
examples: Her tenacity helped her crack the RBI Grade B exam after four attempts.
The mountaineer's tenacity in the face of freezing winds got him to the summit at last.

meaning: Very weak or slight
trick: 'Thin'+'uous' — Thin (पतला) धागा = कमज़ोर।
examples: The connection between the two events is tenuous at best.
The explorers' hold on the cliff was tenuous, resting on a single rusty peg.

meaning: Showing or suffering from nervousness or fear
trick: 'Timid'+'ous' — बहुत ज़्यादा Timid (डरपोक)।
examples: The timorous clerk refused to speak up in the heated meeting.
The timorous kitten hid under the sofa whenever the doorbell rang.

meaning: To excite or arouse mildly, often in a superficial way
trick: 'Tickle'+'late' — Tickle (गुदगुदी) से उत्तेजित करना।
examples: The gossip columns are designed to titillate readers with scandalous details.
Cheap tabloids titillate readers with half-true stories about the private lives of film stars.

meaning: Lacking energy or alertness; sluggish
trick: 'तोड़'+'पड़ा' — थककर टूटा पड़ा = सुस्त, निष्क्रिय।
examples: The torpid market showed no movement even during trading hours.
In the midday heat, the torpid snake lay motionless on the warm rock.

meaning: Full of twists and turns; complex
trick: 'Torture'+'ous' — Torture (यातना) देने वाला घुमावदार रास्ता।
examples: The tortuous legal process frustrated the small investor.
The tortuous mountain path doubled back on itself so often that the travellers lost their sense of direction.

meaning: The path followed by an object, or the development curve of something
trick: 'Tractor' — ट्रैक्टर खेत में अपना रास्ता बनाता है।
examples: The country's growth trajectory looks highly positive.
The cricket ball followed a high trajectory before landing safely beyond the boundary rope.

meaning: Lasting only a short time; temporary
trick: 'Train'+'Saint' — ट्रेन और साधु स्टेशन पर थोड़ी देर के लिए ही रुकते हैं।
examples: The central bank believes the current spike in food prices is transient.
The transient visitors stayed only a night at the inn before moving on.

meaning: Vigorous and incisive in expression
trick: 'Trench'+'Ant' — Trench (गहरा गड्ढा) खोदने वाली तीखी बात।
examples: The editorial offered a trenchant critique of the bank's lending policy.
The critic's trenchant review of the play left the director with little to defend.

meaning: A feeling of fear or agitation about something that may happen
trick: 'Trip'+'Date'+'ion' — Date पर Trip करने से पहले की घबराहट।
examples: She waited for the final exam result with trepidation.
With trepidation, the young soldier stepped forward to deliver the bad news to his commander.

meaning: Eager to argue or fight; aggressively defiant
trick: 'Truck'+'Ulta' — सड़क पर ट्रक उल्टा हो गया तो ड्राइवर झगड़ा करने पर उतारू हो गया।
examples: His truculent attitude during negotiations ruined the business deal.
The truculent drunk picked a quarrel with every passenger on the late bus.

meaning: To shorten by cutting off a part
trick: 'Trunk'+'Cut' — Trunk (तना) को Cut करके छोटा कर देना।
examples: The report had to be truncated to fit within presentation time.
The editor had to truncate the interview to make it fit into half a page.

meaning: Full of confusion or disorder
trick: 'Tu'+'Multi' — तू-तू मैं-मैं और Multiple लोगों का शोर = उथल-पुथल।
examples: The banking sector experienced a tumultuous year due to global rate hikes.
The tumultuous welcome at the airport, with drums and flowers, delighted the returning champions.

meaning: Swollen; pompous or overblown in style
trick: 'Tyre'+'gid' — हवा भरकर फूला Tyre; वैसी ही फूली- भारी, बोझिल भाषा।
examples: The speech was so turgid that half the audience lost interest.
The turgid river swelled with monsoon rain and spilled across the fields.

meaning: Wicked or corrupt behavior
trick: 'Tur'+'Pit'+'ude' — Pit (गड्ढा) में गिराने वाला बुरा काम।
examples: Moral turpitude is a valid ground for immediate dismissal from bank service.
The court dismissed the lawyer from the bar for an act of moral turpitude.

meaning: Protection of or authority over someone; instruction
trick: 'Tutor'+'Age' — Tutor की देखरेख वाली Age, यानी मार्गदर्शन और संरक्षण।
examples: Under the tutelage of the senior manager, she quickly learned the ropes.
Under the gentle tutelage of an old master, the boy learned to carve fine wooden toys.

meaning: Present everywhere at the same time
trick: 'Uber' — Uber की गाड़ियाँ हर जगह मिलती हैं।
examples: UPI payments have become ubiquitous in India.
Mobile phones are ubiquitous now, found in the hands of farmers, students and shopkeepers alike.

meaning: A neighbor whose house is on fire
trick: 'You' + 'Call' + 'Gone' — आपके पड़ोसी का घर जल गया, अब आपको बुला रहा है।
examples: The ucalegon frantically knocked on the doors to warn everyone about the fire.
The ucalegon stood in his nightclothes on the street, watching flames swallow his home while neighbours rushed to help.

meaning: The amount by which a container is empty
trick: 'Hollow'+'age' — टैंक या बोतल का Hollow (खाली) हिस्सा।
examples: The ullage in the tank was measured before filling it with fuel.
The wine merchant noted the ullage in each barrel to see how much had evaporated.

meaning: Existing beyond what is obvious; hidden
trick: 'Ultra'+'erior' — Ultra (आगे) क्या छिपा है, वो छुपा इरादा।
examples: He suspected that his colleague had an ulterior motive behind the help.
The salesman's friendly chat had an ulterior purpose: he wanted to sell her an expensive policy.

meaning: The darkest part of a shadow
trick: 'Umbrella' — Umbrella की छाया जैसा गहरा अंधेरा।
examples: The lunar eclipse showed the umbra of the earth covering the moon completely.
During the solar eclipse, villagers standing in the moon's umbra experienced total darkness at noon.

meaning: Offense or annoyance at something perceived as insulting
trick: 'Umbrella'+'Rage' — किसी ने मेरा Umbrella छीना तो मुझे Rage (नाराज़गी) आ गई।
examples: She took umbrage at the manager's rude remarks during the audit.
The chef took umbrage at the critic's remark and refused to serve him again.

hindi: बिना रुके / लगातार / तीव्र गति से जारी
meaning: Continuing without any reduction in intensity
trick: 'Un'+'A-bait' (बैठ) — जो कभी बैठे/थमे नहीं, बिना रुके लगातार जारी रहे।
examples: Demand for luxury housing continued unabated despite higher interest rates.
The storm raged unabated through the night, tearing roofs off the fishermen's huts.

meaning: Strange or mysterious in an unsettling way
trick: 'Un'+'Can' — जिसे Explain न कर Can, ऐसा अजीब और रहस्यमय।
examples: She has an uncanny ability to predict market trends.
There was an uncanny resemblance between the two strangers, as if they were twins.

meaning: Unreasonably excessive or morally wrong
trick: 'Un'+'Conscience' — जिसका कोई Conscience (ज़मीर) न हो।
examples: Charging 80% interest on a small loan is an unconscionable practice.
Making workers toil sixteen hours a day without pay is unconscionable.

hindi: चापलूसी वाला / चिकनी-चुपड़ी बातें करने वाला
meaning: Insincerely flattering; oily in manner
trick: 'Uncle'+'Chai' — जो अंकल को बार-बार चाय पिलाकर मक्खन लगाए वो चापलूस है।
examples: The salesman made an unctuous attempt to win the client's favor.
The unctuous waiter bowed repeatedly and praised every dish in a greasy voice.

meaning: To support or strengthen from below
trick: 'Under'+'Pin' — नीचे से Pin लगाकर किसी चीज़ को मज़बूत सहारा देना।
examples: Strong agricultural output helps underpin the rural economy.
Strong roots underpin the old oak, letting it stand against every storm.

meaning: To guarantee financial support or insurance
trick: 'Under'+'Write' — पर्ची के Under अपना नाम Write करके गारंटी देना।
examples: The bank agreed to underwrite the new bond issue.
A wealthy patron agreed to underwrite the cost of printing the poet's first book.

meaning: To move in a wave-like pattern

The sharp-tongued traveller mocked the yokel for gaping at the tall buildings, though the villager only smiled.

meaning: At some distance in the direction indicated
trick: 'Wonder' — दूर पहाड़ के उस पार एक Wonder है।
examples: The village lies yonder, beyond those green hills.
Look at the smoke rising from yonder hill, where the shepherds have lit their evening fire.

meaning: Of long ago; in the past
trick: 'Your'+'e' — Your (तुम्हारे) पुराने ज़माने की बातें।
examples: In days of yore, bankers kept ledgers handwritten in thick books.
Tales of yore describe kings who rode through the forest to listen to the troubles of their subjects.

meaning: Amusingly unconventional and idiosyncratic
trick: 'Zany' ~ 'सनकी' — सनकी, अजीब और मज़ाकिया।
examples: His zany antics at the office party kept everyone in splits.
The zany comedian juggled eggs while riding a tiny bicycle, and the children shrieked with laughter.

meaning: Great energy or enthusiasm for a cause
trick: 'Jail' — देश के लिए जेल जाने का गजब का जोश और उत्साह।
examples: He started his new job at the bank with unmatched zeal and energy.
The volunteers planted saplings along the highway with such zeal that the work finished in a single weekend.

meaning: A person who is fanatical about a cause
trick: 'Zeal' — जो धुन के पक्के जोशीले इंसान से भी बढ़कर हो।
examples: The zealot refused to listen to any view other than his own.
The religious zealot stood in the market shouting that anyone who disagreed with him was doomed.

meaning: Filled with great energy and enthusiasm
trick: 'Zeal' — जो अपने काम को लेकर पूरे जोश और उत्साह से भरा हो।
examples: The zealous new recruits completed their training targets ahead of time.
The zealous young detective checked every footprint and fingerprint, determined not to miss a single clue.

meaning: The dominant spirit or mood of a period
trick: 'Time'+'Ghost' — समय का Ghost यानी उस ज़माने की आत्मा।
examples: The app captured the zeitgeist of the digital age perfectly.
The songs of that decade captured the zeitgeist of a generation that longed for peace and change.

meaning: The highest point of something
trick: 'ज़ीना' (सीढ़ी) — ज़ीने की सबसे ऊपरी सीढ़ी = शिखर।
examples: His career reached its zenith when he became the RBI Governor.
At noon the sun reaches its zenith, and the shadows beneath the trees shrink to almost nothing.

meaning: A soft gentle breeze
trick: 'ज़रा फिर' — ज़रा फिर से वो हल्की ठंडी हवा चलाओ!
examples: The zephyr of reform brought fresh hope to the banking sector.
A cool zephyr drifted through the open window, rustling the pages of her notebook.

meaning: Relating to a gentle breeze
trick: 'Zephyr' (हल्की हवा) — Zephyr जैसी मुलायम और सुहावनी।
examples: The zephyrean evening breeze made the lakeside walk unforgettable.
Poets praised the zephyrean whispers that stirred the curtains on the warm summer afternoon.

meaning: A large dirigible airship
trick: 'Zip'+'Balloon' — Zip वाला बहुत बड़ा Balloon जो हवा में उड़े।
examples: The zeppelin offered a luxurious but slow way to travel across the ocean.
In the 1930s, wealthy passengers boarded a giant zeppelin in Germany and floated gently toward America.

meaning: An ancient Mesopotamian temple tower
trick: 'Zig'+'gurat' — Zigzag सीढ़ियों वाला विशाल प्राचीन मंदिर।
examples: The ancient ziggurat remains one of the most impressive archaeological sites.
Archaeologists climbed the crumbling steps of the ziggurat, built thousands of years ago in the land of Sumer.

meaning: An animal that resembles a plant, like a coral
trick: 'Zoo' (जानवर) + 'Phyte' (पौधा) — जो दिखे पौधे जैसा पर असल में जानवर हो।
examples: Corals are zoophytes that support entire underwater ecosystems.
Divers marvelled at the zoophyte clinging to the reef, a creature that looked like a flower but fed like an animal.
